# Summary

Subject model Candidate #11

## Question

What is the next Subject model after separating containment/grouping from specialization?

## Status and authority

Candidate #11 is a Specification Proposal, not an adopted source migration or a rebuilt Projection. It refines Candidate #10 rather than replacing its accepted meanings. A1233 records the Operator's explicit decision: Project Model CONTAINS Actor; display this as Project Model > Actor, not a narrower-kind slash link.

The remaining edges below are source-backed proposals for consistent application of that distinction. They are not a claim that every edge was separately approved. Current RMED remains unchanged; the four Draft successors linked by A1233 are still Drafts.

## Relations and notation

- `>` means CONTAINS: organizational membership or an actual whole/part relation in its declared context. It supplies no property inheritance.
- `/` means broader-to-narrower classification in this proposed outline. Inheritance requires an actual source-backed specialization, not display ancestry.
- `.` retains bearer/dependent-property meaning.
- `:` retains allowed-value/qualified-kind meaning, not an instance assignment.
- `//` retains named-instance meaning; instances are not expanded in this candidate.

Keep IS_CONTAINED_BY as the authored direct direction and CONTAINS as its derived inverse. This candidate changes no relation direction or endpoint permission by notation alone. A type may permit containment without requiring every instance to have a contained part; cardinality remains a separate rule.

## Proposed primary outline

Labels are compact. Defining references are bare R IDs only; no Claim text is copied. `<Project Name>` is a namespace pattern, not an instance. The outline shows selected organizational and specialization links, not every relation in the graph.

```text

	> CAPRMEDIO [CA-R-2206]
		> Graph [CA-R-2208]
			> Node [CA-R-1994]
```

## Important boundaries

- Project Model contains vocabulary entries for project things. Its Actor member is not a narrower Project Model kind and inherits no properties through that membership.
- The former Aspect branches organize topics. Engineering > Authoring > Code Authoring is topical grouping here, not automatic inheritance of object properties. Exact deeper topic links remain migration candidates rather than a blanket slash replacement.
- Implementation contains actual implementation material. Its Code branch groups existing Code subjects; it does not require every implementation to use every listed unit kind. Code remains distinct from a File Carrier or Directory Carrier.
- `Package > Module`, `Document > Section` and `Journal > Event Record` retain their source-supported part meanings. A particular Module may contain Functions; a Function is not therefore a narrower Module. The Journal/record meaning does not create a new primary Subject identity in this outline.
- A File is a narrower Carrier kind. A Directory containing a File and a Git Repository containing a Git Branch are independent containment relations. There is no blanket permission or requirement for every Carrier to contain another Carrier.
- Actor specializations use `Actor/AI Agent` and `Actor/Operator` directly; no `Type:` qualifier is used in this branch. Atom and Scope Unit kinds retain their complete classification syntax. A bare Content Role or Type axis is a Subject/parameter, not an extra inheriting entity. Do not replace `Atom/Content Role: Plan` with `Atom > Content Role > Plan`.
- Scope Unit is also explicitly a Continuant in R1757. It can participate in that classification while retaining its organizational position under Project Model. Multiple typed links do not create multiple Subject identities.
- Event/Execution/Session denote actual happenings; their records remain separate. Runtime denotes a live context. The old Runtime children Container Run/Process Run require a bounded check against their execution definitions before relocation; this candidate does not infer that they are Runtime subtypes from the old slash paths.
- Documentation under Aspect is an authoring/organization topic; Documentation under Implementation is actual content. Their names do not merge their identities.

## Scope and migration boundary

No named instances, property inventory, new Domain entity, generic Node.Type, Revision entity, Scope Unit reorganization, Terms Graph implementation or production Tool/runtime change is introduced.

The compact outline is not a replacement canonical-ID syntax. Source Subjects keep complete canonical selectors; abbreviated labels do not rename targets. The eventual migration needs a thin table: Atom ID | old Subject | new Subject | status. Resolve exact selectors and grouping links before changing sources; do not infer containment from folders or silently replace every slash.

## Existing Drafts and review follow-up

[A1233](CA-A-1233-SPECIFICATION_PROPOSAL--use-containment-for-organizational-subject-grouping.md) records the accepted containment decision and four prepared successors: R2209@3-draft, R1931@13-draft, R2150@11-draft and R2222@2-draft. They are not promoted.

This proposal supplies the structural correction direction for SG3-I02. It does not claim to resolve the other review findings: incorrect defining references, symbolic Tier vocabulary, omitted Relation Type directions, inconsistent formal-rule paths, or the eleven unresolved Relation Type names. Those retain their separate findings and proposed corrections. No new FPF review or authoritative migration has run for Candidate #11.

## Actor specialization decision

[A1235](done/CA-A-1235-SPECIFICATION_PROPOSAL--use-direct-actor-kind-paths.md) records the Operator's correction: `Actor / AI Agent` and `Actor / Operator`. These are narrower Actor kinds, not contained parts or named instances. This supersedes the Actor/Type: notation in the previous candidate only; it does not remove other Type or Content Role qualifiers. Candidate editing is not adoption of new Subjects in Current RMED.

### Summary

Track Entity candidate implementation Questions

## Latest candidate

[CA-A-1302 — Entity graph candidate with four root branches](draft/CA-A-1302@1-draft-SPECIFICATION_PROPOSAL--entity-graph-candidate-with-four-root-branches.md), with A1303/A1304 refinements. The Operator’s latest words override older decisions; implementation evidence uses only the last 48 hours. This proposal tracks every Question created while implementing CA-P-2683.

## Questions and chosen continuation

- [CA-C-605 — Where should Term and Selection belong under Entity?](../01_concern/CA-C-605-QUESTION--where-should-term-and-selection-belong-under-entity.md): Keep the existing persistent Term and Selection classifications under Object/Continuant for this migration. This preserves the latest explicit lower-level tree instead of adding a fifth root. The four-root candidate left their exact placement open; this choice is provisional and does not implement the Terms Graph.

- [CA-C-606 — Does a zero-direct-value property need a value Format?](../01_concern/CA-C-606-QUESTION--does-a-zero-direct-value-property-need-a-value-format.md): For a grouping property with cardinality {0}, state that a direct-value Format is not applicable; define the Formats of its children independently. Do not invent void/list/map as Formats. This reconciles the required property coverage with the approved direct-value semantics.

## Boundaries

The six legacy Graph Rule Subject paths are held for source-specific preservation/retirement during the Definition pass. Missing-ID legacy RMED carriers without Subjects are explicitly unchanged in the Subject-only pass. Neither creates a new entity or requires Engine changes. The Current frontier is 1,100 RMED carriers; 17 legacy records have no explicit Atom ID or Subjects. Existing archived/draft carriers and Engine sources are excluded.

- [CA-C-607 — legacy generic Node/Project Model targets](../01_concern/CA-C-607-QUESTION--which-targets-replace-generic-node-and-project-model-subjects.md): use Entity for the old generic Subject/Node, and Object/Continuant for the persistent grouping during the mechanical pass; narrow or retire actual defining sources during coverage.

- [CA-C-608 — duplicate Terms Projection kind](../01_concern/CA-C-608-QUESTION--does-terms-projection-need-a-separate-kind.md): reuse existing Projection/Type: Terms Graph; leave the duplicate Draft unpromoted. Terms Graph implementation remains deferred.

## Stage 3 chosen continuations

- [CA-C-609 — Should all derived reverse views have a name?](../01_concern/CA-C-609-QUESTION--should-all-derived-reverse-views-have-a-name.md): Keep the direct Relation Types and derive their reverse lookup. Preserve already declared inverse names such as CONTAINS, BEARS and IS_CARRIED_BY. Do not invent a second name or stored fact where the Current definition declares no inverse name. This supplies every reverse view without introducing aliases. The open choice is whether those unnamed views need separate names later.

- [CA-C-610 — Which Runtime owns automatic context initialization?](../01_concern/CA-C-610-QUESTION--which-runtime-owns-automatic-context-initialization.md): Preserve legacy REQU-507's automatic session/context initialization commitment as a framework outcome, rather than dropping it for a malformed header. Use the existing Runtime/Session vocabulary and leave its concrete implementation owner to the later Engine Epic. This does not add a Session Engine entity or implement startup code.

- [CA-C-611 — How should installed Extension lifecycle be represented?](../01_concern/CA-C-611-QUESTION--how-should-installed-extension-lifecycle-be-represented.md): Preserve legacy REQU-697's install, uninstall, update and downgrade commitment. Govern the framework capability and refer to the existing installed-Extensions Scope Units; do not introduce another Extension object or application-binding system. Concrete execution belongs to the later Engine work.

- [CA-C-612 — generic Execution Result value Format](../01_concern/CA-C-612-QUESTION--how-should-unconstrained-execution-result-values-be-formatted.md): use the reusable scalar Format and direct-value cardinality; retain producer-specific output constraints.

## Property and Relation completion choices

- [CA-C-613 — Confirm minimal shared Property value schemas](../01_concern/CA-C-613-QUESTION--confirm-minimal-shared-property-value-schemas.md): The implementation uses string for identifiers/names/locators, integers for counts, optional explicit Scope Unit Label, and one or more string values for an ordered Scope Unit Path. Settings/registry/configuration groups have zero direct scalar values; their children keep independent counts. Producer- or invocation-specific properties read within their defining Claim scope. These choices complete the existing model without new stored fields or advanced conditions; change them only if a concrete source requires a different shape.

- [CA-C-614 — Does a concrete Relation connection need a separate kind?](../01_concern/CA-C-614-QUESTION--does-a-concrete-relation-connection-need-a-separate-kind.md): For now an actual directed connection remains the tuple (source, Relation Type, target), without a new Connection entity or separate ID. R2247 preserves source/target reference meanings; R1986 and R1987 were retired because those are not reusable Type metadata. Existing direct facts and derived inverses stay governed. A separate endpoint-record kind can be reconsidered only if a concrete operation needs it.

## Actual readback reference disposition

- [CA-C-615](../01_concern/CA-C-615-QUESTION--should-legacy-concern-resolution-links-be-restored-as-history.md): Remove the three unresolvable legacy resolution_of links from Current R1646, R1647 and R1648. Their Current Claims remain unchanged; the exact former links remain in the newly preserved predecessors and Journal history. Do not invent canonical Concern IDs or migrate C/A. If those old Concern records are recovered, consider source-traceable historical references rather than guessing a Current native target.

## Delivery classification continuation

- [CA-C-616](../01_concern/CA-C-616-QUESTION--should-delivery-policy-ownership-require-child-scope-units.md): Use the latest reusable D Policy versus individual D Decision distinction for the Core representation rules. A Core D Policy can govern an Object/property kind across applicable cases without its owning Scope Unit having children. Preserve the actual-child condition on Method Eng Policy. This avoids inventing Scope Units solely to allow the explicitly requested Core D Policies.

## Governing-configuration boundary

- [CA-C-617](../01_concern/CA-C-617-QUESTION--where-should-stable-scope-unit-ids-be-carried.md): Keep the adopted logical Scope Unit.ID definition and its string cardinality, but preserve the existing governing-configuration bytes and registered Scope Unit Name references. R1988 expressly adds no storage field or rename procedure; the latest 48-hour decisions do not specify a concrete migration protocol. Do not invent a new TOML key, allocate IDs to excluded Engine Scope Units, or revise the Scope Unit structure in this methodology-only Epic. Define the concrete ID encoding/data migration in the already separate Engine/Scope Unit work before requiring it from those readers.

# Summary

Subject model Candidate #10

## Question

What is the proposed main Subject structure, and which R Atom defines each primary entity or topic?

## Content Scope

Main structure and definitions only. No instances, property lists, instance names, actual Relation Type or Graph Rule instances, source migration or implementation. Namespace and topic headings are explicitly distinguished from independently modeled things.

## Proposal

This Specification Proposal records the accepted design and decisions. Its reviewed definitions and Subject mappings are now adopted in Current RMED. Those source Atoms remain authoritative; this Analysis is not their replacement or the rebuilt Projection.

```text
			/Relation  [CA-R-1963]
			/Rule  [CA-R-1995]
		/Carrier  [CA-R-1958]
	/<Project Name>  [namespace pattern; CA-R-2207 governs Subject]
```

`<Project Name>` describes a namespace pattern; it is not an instantiated project Subject. CAPRMEDIO is the shared framework vocabulary namespace. Projects use that vocabulary and add their own Subjects without copying it. Namespace, Graph and Project Model headings organize the vocabulary; they do not assert that every child is a subtype of a new real-world entity.

Event and Execution retain existing meanings rather than disappearing during regrouping. History/Journal/Release describe preserved material, while Event, Execution and Runtime describe actual occurrences or contexts. Implementation is directly edited and is not a Projection.

## Definition boundaries

- Project Model names project things, including Implementation. Aspects name topics addressing those things. CAPRMEDO Atoms and I Implementation are different structures inside the model; not every Project Model item is an Atom.
- Content Role is a classification axis and remains a valid Subject; it is not another primary entity between Atom and role-qualified Atom kinds. The R1531 Draft defines this distinction. No role values or instances are expanded in this main tree.
- A Carrier is distinct from what it represents. A graph can represent a Carrier as a node without merging representation with represented content.
- Documentation under Implementation is actual content; Documentation under Aspect is the topic governing its organization and authoring.
- Subject, Content Role and owning Scope Unit stay independent. A shared Subject does not become project-specific because its governing Atom lives in Project Configuration.
- This proposal does not reintroduce Revision, property entities, generic Graph Node.Type, or Terms-Graph work. Existing Continuant/Occurrent definitions remain available, but their temporal classifications are not mandatory path layers in this proposed main outline.

## Review boundaries and open points

The proposed graph and namespace groupings are organizational levels, not automatically NARROWER_THAN edges. The completed bounded review found no concern from the outline alone; it did not establish complete grammar admission. The project-name placeholder does not choose name normalization or collision/rename handling. These are unresolved proposal details, not new runtime requirements. Existing Entity terminology is preserved rather than silently retired. Existing Term paths are relocated under Project Model/Term; Terms Graph work stays deferred.

## Work and decisions

Subject model Candidate #10

## Question

What is the proposed main Subject structure, and which R Atom defines each primary entity or topic?

## Content Scope

Main structure and definitions only. No instances, property lists, instance names, actual Relation Type or Graph Rule instances, source migration or implementation. Namespace and topic headings are explicitly distinguished from independently modeled things.

## Proposal

This Specification Proposal records the accepted design and decisions. Its reviewed definitions and Subject mappings are now adopted in Current RMED. Those source Atoms remain authoritative; this Analysis is not their replacement or the rebuilt Projection.

```text
			/Rule  [CA-R-1995]
		/Carrier  [CA-R-1958]
	/<Project Name>  [namespace pattern; CA-R-2207 governs Subject]
```

`<Project Name>` describes a namespace pattern; it is not an instantiated project Subject. CAPRMEDIO is the shared framework vocabulary namespace. Projects use that vocabulary and add their own Subjects without copying it. Namespace, Graph and Project Model headings organize the vocabulary; they do not assert that every child is a subtype of a new real-world entity.

Event and Execution retain existing meanings rather than disappearing during regrouping. History/Journal/Release describe preserved material, while Event, Execution and Runtime describe actual occurrences or contexts. Implementation is directly edited and is not a Projection.

## Definition boundaries

- Project Model names project things, including Implementation. Aspects name topics addressing those things. CAPRMEDO Atoms and I Implementation are different structures inside the model; not every Project Model item is an Atom.
- Content Role is a classification axis and remains a valid Subject; it is not another primary entity between Atom and role-qualified Atom kinds. The R1531 Draft defines this distinction. No role values or instances are expanded in this main tree.
- A Carrier is distinct from what it represents. A graph can represent a Carrier as a node without merging representation with represented content.
- Documentation under Implementation is actual content; Documentation under Aspect is the topic governing its organization and authoring.
- Subject, Content Role and owning Scope Unit stay independent. A shared Subject does not become project-specific because its governing Atom lives in Project Configuration.
- This proposal does not reintroduce Revision, property entities, generic Graph Node.Type, or Terms-Graph work. Existing Continuant/Occurrent definitions remain available, but their temporal classifications are not mandatory path layers in this proposed main outline.

The proposed graph and namespace groupings are organizational levels, not automatically NARROWER_THAN edges. The completed bounded review found no concern from the outline alone; it did not establish complete grammar admission. The project-name placeholder does not choose name normalization or collision/rename handling. These are unresolved proposal details, not new runtime requirements. # Summary

Model draft: primary kinds and properties

## Status and scope

Review Draft extending Candidate #12 (CA-A-1238). The latest Operator naming decision is Model, replacing the earlier name Formal Model. Prepared selectors use Model::...; Current sources are not migrated by this proposal. Its five base branches are Continuant, Occurrent, Aspect, Carrier and Graph Syntax. Relation and value Format are grouped under Graph Syntax. Structural constraints belong to model Definition Claims, not a separate Graph Rule branch or instance population. Project Model is only an optional organizational view, not a base classification.

This Draft contains the primary tree, then one flat property block for every selected primary kind with known direct or inherited properties, in the same declaration order as the tree. It includes no named instances. It does not promote Drafts, migrate Current Atoms, rename YAML fields or change code. Terms Graph work and the function proposals in CA-A-1237 remain deferred.

Each property block shows its proposed full `subjects.governs` selector. These describe the proposed governing targets; they are not claims that existing source Atom headers already use the new paths. Inline cardinality/format annotations belong to Claims, not to these selectors.

## Reading the annotations

- `/` specializes; `::` groups; `>` contains, and each contained part belongs to exactly one whole; `@(...)` refers to an existing declaration. `((RELATION_TYPE))` names a defined Relation without a short operator. Only actual specialization carries inherited properties.
- `[int]`, `[string]`, `[bool]`, `[datetime]`, `[decimal]` and `[float]` name proposed value formats. Format is for value types only. List and map are carrier structures, not value Formats; child paths define nesting under CA-A-1283 and CA-A-1286. Carrier.Format continues to describe representation formats; Markdown/YAML/TOML/JSON are not placed under this new Format branch.
- General formula and function-style expressions are deferred to CA-A-1282. Existing-kind `@(...)` references remain; general property-value interpolation and executable composition do not enter this syntax increment. A1291 remains a separate bracketed-condition proposal, excluded from this review under A1297.
- Cardinalities under CA-A-1280: `{n}` means exactly n; `{n+}` means at least n without an upper bound; `{n..m}` is an inclusive range. Bounds are non-negative integers with n <= m. Common forms are `{0}`, `{1}`, `{0+}`, `{1+}` and `{0..1}`. A property suffix counts only its own direct values, never nested keys or child values; explicit `{0}` permits a grouping path with independently counted children; `>{1+}` and `>{0+}` count immediate parts per whole. Omitted counts remain unspecified; explicit `{0}` is used for grouping properties. No parser implementation is claimed.
- `[inherited]` marks actual specialization inheritance. Grouping and containment do not supply it. A local additive Status declaration retains inherited values.
- Omitted format or cardinality is undefined in this declaration. In particular, subjects without a suffix is not subjects{0}, subjects{1} or subjects{0+}. Explicit counts remain distinct; independently applicable rules still apply. CA-A-1284 records this distinction. Definition and rule references use Atom IDs only; no definition text is copied into the tree.
- Format annotations are proposed readable constraints unless a cited rule explicitly specifies the datatype. CA-A-1287 removes ref as a value Format. Reference-valued identifiers use string; their definitions preserve target meanings such as Actor, Scope Unit, Operator and Project. Existing-kind @ references are separate syntax and remain admitted.
- Base counts describe the complete-Atom contract, with the Claim structure in CA-A-1243 and the R-only formalization scope in CA-A-1244. Every complete RMED Atom has content.claim{1}. Only R admits an optional content.claim.formal_claim{0..1} child, alongside its mandatory direct prose. The formal child cannot satisfy the prose count. M/E/D keep prose Claims. The Role/Type defines what forms one complete Claim. No separate atom.claim/formal_claim or content.claim.prose field is used. Drafts may be incomplete. Project Goal ownership remains exceptional. Effective Label is required, but its stored explicit value is optional and falls back to Type.

## Cardinality notation

| Notation | Meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{n}` | Exactly n | `{1}`: exactly one |
| `{n+}` | At least n, no upper bound | `{2+}`: two or more |
| `{n..m}` | From n to m, inclusive | `{2..5}`: two through five |
| `{0}` | No direct values or no contained parts | A group can still have declared child properties |
| `{0+}` | Zero or more direct values or parts | An optional multi-value property |
| `{1+}` | One or more | At least one part or value |
| `{0..1}` | Zero or one | An optional single value |
| `{0..m}` | At most m | `{0..3}`: zero through three |

The suffix counts only direct values at that path, or immediate parts per whole after >. It never counts nested keys. Grouping subjects{0} permits governs{1} and dependency{0+} as independently counted children. YAML sequences carry multiple values under one unique property key; list is not a value Format. The exactly-one immediate whole rule is unchanged. CA-A-1283 records this decision.

## Deferred formula proposal

General formula expressions are preserved separately in [CA-A-1282](../CA-A-1282-SPECIFICATION_PROPOSAL--defer-general-formula-expressions.md), rather than admitted in this Model Draft. This includes composed ID values, property-value interpolation, formula grouping, function-style uniqueness expressions and calculated counts. Existing scalar IDs and their governing prose rules remain unchanged. Bracketed conditions and implicit value materialization remain separate proposals under A1291, outside the current review. The explicit execution function remains deferred. Cardinalities, formats, literal allowed values, relationship operators and existing-kind references stay in scope.

## Property and rule qualifications

Under A1296, YAML null and an empty string each count as one direct value; an omitted property has zero. YAML interpretation determines the value. Its Format and applicable prose conditions decide admissibility; the count alone does not. There is no universal null or empty-string prohibition.

Subject values use string under CA-A-1285. The basic format check validates the string and its admitted Model notation without requiring the target to pre-exist its defining Atom. A Definition may introduce its entity and governed path together. Syntax alone does not define the entity or grant authority.

- `id` and `version_number` use the Operator's latest example spellings. They do not rename `atom_id` or `version` in YAML. Use atom.version_number for the YAML part and atom.content.claim for the Markdown part. No atom.property, property/text subgroup or colon-based lookup layer is introduced.
- Version Number is positive and increases for updates. Tier uses [int] in this review packet. Its lower bound is -1; the numeric and more-specific conditions stay in prose under A1297: Project ordinary >=0, other ordinary >=1, Project Goal -1 with Operator ownership. No case-specific lookup function or conditional expression is needed. Numbers are graph ordering, not a second Global Tier.
- RMED content.claim_scope can be omitted only when the Claim covers the whole governed thing/topic and whole owning context. Conditional requirements still apply to a property shown as 0..1. Other Content Roles retain their registered scope contract.
- Analysis Question/Analysis counts depend on its applicable Type. Analysis Done is admitted by the applicable Analysis Report/Rationale rules, not asserted as a new universal Status on every Analysis Type.
- Every complete RMED Atom carries exactly one content.claim. Its own direct text is one required prose value. Only R admits optional content.claim.formal_claim with one fenced formal expression for now; M/E/D stay prose, including their syntax/format/relation policies and decisions. Illustrative code does not create an operative formal child. A Definition may combine required prose and optional complementary formal structure as one Type-defined unit, not separate Atoms for each representation or condition. Semantics is outside Claim and adds no operative constraints.
- The RMED section order is ## Summary, optional ## Claim scope, required ## Claim, optional ## Semantics, optional ## Details. R alone may add optional ### Formal claim under Claim. The Summary value is below ## Summary, not substituted into the heading. Optional sections are omitted when absent. A formal child needs a defined syntax/schema. All top-level RMED sections are siblings at ##; Summary never contains Claim. Heading hierarchy maps Claim → Formal claim to content.claim.formal_claim; normalized components are lowercase with spaces replaced by underscores and characters other than letters, numbers, underscore and hyphen stripped.
- Enabled Relations.Contains is a kind-level capability, with base default False and Plan/Workflow/Step enabling True. It is not a mandatory Boolean field to add to every Atom instance. The existing Step rule CA-R-1992 still describes nested Steps; this Draft retains its enabling value but follows the Operator's newer distinct-Substep decision for the contained kind.
- The Project Goal Owner targets Operator, Target Scope Unit targets Project, and its single Tier is exactly -1. Its absence of Local Scope Unit is the explicit exception, not permission to omit that field on ordinary Atoms.
- Governing Objects classifies Atom and Governing Configuration without granting additional authority to any Content Role. Structural Unit classifies Scope Unit; Project specializes Scope Unit and is its single parentless root. Scope Units recursively contain Scope Units and may contain Atom/Projection parts. No numeric structural rank or ownership-field rename is introduced by these groups.
- Event Record is declared only under History/Journal. Project Implementation specializes Package and is the root Package. Implementation is only a section heading. Package contains nested Packages, Modules, Prompts, runtime/evaluation Assets and Documentation; Code Units belong inside Modules, with Class and Function specializations. There is no separate Code kind in this proposed model. Prompt is executable instructions for an LLM AI Agent engine; Module is executable on its language engine; both runtime code and evaluation code, including tests, are Modules. Asset is non-executable Implementation content needed by runtime or evaluations. Documentation provides descriptive/reference information separately from those required inputs. Neither definition automatically captures every non-executable repository file. Module's one File Carrier and Package's proposed Directory representation remain distinct Delivery concerns. Documentation is a Package part separate from Asset. Resources is retired in this proposal under CA-A-1278; its non-executable implementation inputs specialize Asset. Containment does not confer property inheritance.
- Projection remains a direct Continuant and Terms Projection specializes it. Term remains separate as in the Operator's tree. This classification does not create a Terms Projection artifact or start Terms Graph implementation.
- Carrier, Actor, Execution, Project, History, Projection and their descendants do not inherit Scope Unit fields through the former Project Model grouping. The old projection's spurious Scope Unit subtree is excluded.
- Current source rules and operative formal graph-rule paths still use older Subject paths. This review Draft does not claim those paths were migrated to Model.

## Deferred or unresolved details

- Format has a new Definition Draft; individual primitive-format definitions remain to be completed before adoption. This Draft does not assert a closed primitive vocabulary, specific numeric precision, float special-value policy or reference encoding.
- Formula design and property-value bindings remain outside this adoption increment under CA-A-1282. A1295 permits future functions only when recurring patterns establish reusable operations that reduce overall complexity; no per-case or per-instance function proliferation is admitted. No new ID component field or contextual named Selection is created.
- Substep is a leaf: it calls one Action with parameters, cannot call a Workflow and cannot contain further Substeps. A leaf Step can call one Action or one Workflow with parameters; a Step containing Substeps has no own call. A1262–A1264 record these decisions. Catalog reconciliation and Substep numeric identity remain preparation work, not an open choice about the settled container hierarchy. Containment supplies no inheritance.
- Code Unit is declared under Module, with Class and Function as specializations. Modules belong to Packages; the former Code-versus-Package question is closed. Package is a declared kind; Project Implementation is its root specialization, not a containing Implementation kind. Tool is not a separate primary kind under CA-A-1273: use Scope Unit instances and existing Package implementation structure. R2197 is a retirement candidate; R2205 meaning is preserved in Engineering API Self Documentation. R2204 Effect Result meaning is mapped to Execution.Result under CA-A-1276; its API result contract stays in Engineering/API. Current retirement is pending. Current source definitions are not deleted by these candidate placements.
- The Operator confirms Workflow >{1+} Step >{0+} Substep. CA-A-1279 reconfirms this settled hierarchy with the latest cardinality spelling. It is prepared in Definition Drafts; Current source adoption is still pending.
- Complete Type inventories and property formats/counts absent from sources remain deferred. Useful legacy graph constraints need incorporation into the appropriate Definition Claims before retiring their Current sources. No Graph Rule instance registry or substitute Rule population is introduced.
- The read-only property inventory retains older direct labels for evidence. Retired Substance, Atom.Entity, duplicate Governed Subject vs Subjects.Governs, and accidental inherited Scope Unit fields are not copied into the Draft. No extra Scope Unit Status or Global Tier is introduced.

## General named relations

`Source ((RELATION_TYPE)) Target` expresses the named directed Relation from Source to Target. Use this general form where no short operator exists; it may also spell a defined Relation explicitly without changing its meaning. The name between `((` and `))` identifies one declared Relation Type, not a new kind, arbitrary prose label or automatically registered Relation. Endpoint restrictions and counts come from the Relation definition and constraints in the relevant Model Definition Claim.

There is no separate backward notation. To navigate or display the opposite direction, use the defined derived inverse Relation name in the same form with the endpoints exchanged. Persist the direct fact only, not a second independent inverse fact. No inverse name or inverse meaning is guessed from spelling.

The matching unescaped `((` and `))` delimit the Relation Type name. Existing backslash escaping handles literal delimiter characters. Existing `/`, `//`, `.`, `:`, `::`, `>`, `@(...)` and format/cardinality annotations keep their meanings. The double parentheses are relation syntax, not a function invocation. This decision defines a binary relation expression; it does not silently choose precedence for arbitrary mixed chains or turn a whole relation statement into a node selector for subjects.governs.

The Operator supplied these schema-level examples:

```text
Workflow Run ((IS_EXECUTION_OF)) Workflow
Event Record ((RECORDS)) Workflow Run
Runtime ((EXECUTES)) Workflow Run
```

These expressions connect modeled kinds and do not create actual Runs or records. Their Relation Type definitions and derived-inverse declarations must be authored before source admission; notation alone does not establish that they are already registered. The Runtime in the last expression is the live executor, not the Engineering topic or stored engine Code.

Decision record: [CA-A-1240](../CA-A-1240-SPECIFICATION_PROPOSAL--use-named-relation-notation.md).

## Definition, execution and record connections

```text
Workflow Run ((IS_EXECUTION_OF)) Workflow
Event Record ((RECORDS)) Workflow Run
```

Every Workflow Run executes exactly one Workflow; this binding is stated in prose rather than an undefined suffix on a named relation. Workflow is the reusable definition; Workflow Run is an actual Occurrent; Event Record is its persistent description in Journal. The displayed RECORDS target is one supported case, not a closed range restricting every record to Workflow Run. The inverse views HAS_EXECUTION and IS_RECORDED_BY are proposed in the two Definition Drafts; direct facts are stored once. No actual Run or record is created here.

## Step and Substep call boundaries

A leaf Step calls one Action or one Workflow with parameters. A Step containing Substeps makes no call of its own. A Substep is a leaf that calls one Action with parameters: no Workflow calls and no nested Substeps.

```text
Workflow >{1+} Step
Step >{0+} Substep
Substep >{0} @(Substep)
```

Containment connects a Workflow to its Steps and a Step to its Substeps. It does not mean the caller contains the called Workflow or Action definition. No wrapper Action or new execution kind is introduced for Workflow calls.

# Summary

Model draft: primary kinds and properties

## Status and scope

Review Draft extending Candidate #12 (CA-A-1238). The latest Operator naming decision is Model, replacing the earlier name Formal Model. Prepared selectors use Model::...; Current sources are not migrated by this proposal. Its five base branches are Continuant, Occurrent, Aspect, Carrier and Graph Syntax. Relation and value Format are grouped under Graph Syntax. Structural constraints belong to model Definition Claims, not a separate Graph Rule branch or instance population. Project Model is only an optional organizational view, not a base classification.

This Draft contains the primary tree, then one flat property block for every selected primary kind with known direct or inherited properties, in the same declaration order as the tree. It includes no named instances. It does not promote Drafts, migrate Current Atoms, rename YAML fields or change code. Terms Graph work and the function proposals in CA-A-1237 remain deferred.

Each property block shows its proposed full `subjects.governs` selector. These describe the proposed governing targets; they are not claims that existing source Atom headers already use the new paths. Inline cardinality/format annotations belong to Claims, not to these selectors.

## Reading the annotations

- `/` specializes; `::` groups; `>` contains, and each contained part belongs to exactly one whole; `@(...)` refers to an existing declaration. `((RELATION_TYPE))` names a defined Relation without a short operator. Only actual specialization carries inherited properties.
- `[int]`, `[string]`, `[bool]`, `[datetime]`, `[decimal]` and `[float]` name proposed value formats. Format is for value types only. List and map are carrier structures, not value Formats; child paths define nesting under CA-A-1283 and CA-A-1286. Carrier.Format continues to describe representation formats; Markdown/YAML/TOML/JSON are not placed under this new Format branch.
- General formula and function-style expressions are deferred to CA-A-1282. Existing-kind `@(...)` references remain; general property-value interpolation and executable composition do not enter this syntax increment. A1291 remains a separate bracketed-condition proposal, excluded from this review under A1297.
- Cardinalities under CA-A-1280: `{n}` means exactly n; `{n+}` means at least n without an upper bound; `{n..m}` is an inclusive range. Bounds are non-negative integers with n <= m. Common forms are `{0}`, `{1}`, `{0+}`, `{1+}` and `{0..1}`. A property suffix counts only its own direct values, never nested keys or child values; explicit `{0}` permits a grouping path with independently counted children; `>{1+}` and `>{0+}` count immediate parts per whole. Omitted counts remain unspecified; explicit `{0}` is used for grouping properties. No parser implementation is claimed.
- `[inherited]` marks actual specialization inheritance. Grouping and containment do not supply it. A local additive Status declaration retains inherited values.
- Omitted format or cardinality is undefined in this declaration. In particular, subjects without a suffix is not subjects{0}, subjects{1} or subjects{0+}. Explicit counts remain distinct; independently applicable rules still apply. CA-A-1284 records this distinction. Definition and rule references use Atom IDs only; no definition text is copied into the tree.
- Format annotations are proposed readable constraints unless a cited rule explicitly specifies the datatype. CA-A-1287 removes ref as a value Format. Reference-valued identifiers use string; their definitions preserve target meanings such as Actor, Scope Unit, Operator and Project. Existing-kind @ references are separate syntax and remain admitted.
- Base counts describe the complete-Atom contract, with the Claim structure in CA-A-1243 and the R-only formalization scope in CA-A-1244. Every complete RMED Atom has content.claim{1}. Only R admits an optional content.claim.formal_claim{0..1} child, alongside its mandatory direct prose. The formal child cannot satisfy the prose count. M/E/D keep prose Claims. The Role/Type defines what forms one complete Claim. No separate atom.claim/formal_claim or content.claim.prose field is used. Drafts may be incomplete. Project Goal ownership remains exceptional. Effective Label is required, but its stored explicit value is optional and falls back to Type.

## Cardinality notation

| Notation | Meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{n}` | Exactly n | `{1}`: exactly one |
| `{n+}` | At least n, no upper bound | `{2+}`: two or more |
| `{n..m}` | From n to m, inclusive | `{2..5}`: two through five |
| `{0}` | No direct values or no contained parts | A group can still have declared child properties |
| `{0+}` | Zero or more direct values or parts | An optional multi-value property |
| `{1+}` | One or more | At least one part or value |
| `{0..1}` | Zero or one | An optional single value |
| `{0..m}` | At most m | `{0..3}`: zero through three |

The suffix counts only direct values at that path, or immediate parts per whole after >. It never counts nested keys. Grouping subjects{0} permits governs{1} and dependency{0+} as independently counted children. YAML sequences carry multiple values under one unique property key; list is not a value Format. The exactly-one immediate whole rule is unchanged. CA-A-1283 records this decision.

## General named relations

`Source ((RELATION_TYPE)) Target` expresses the named directed Relation from Source to Target. Use this general form where no short operator exists; it may also spell a defined Relation explicitly without changing its meaning. The name between `((` and `))` identifies one declared Relation Type, not a new kind, arbitrary prose label or automatically registered Relation. Endpoint restrictions and counts come from the Relation definition and constraints in the relevant Model Definition Claim.

There is no separate backward notation. To navigate or display the opposite direction, use the defined derived inverse Relation name in the same form with the endpoints exchanged. Persist the direct fact only, not a second independent inverse fact. No inverse name or inverse meaning is guessed from spelling.

The matching unescaped `((` and `))` delimit the Relation Type name. Existing backslash escaping handles literal delimiter characters. Existing `/`, `//`, `.`, `:`, `::`, `>`, `@(...)` and format/cardinality annotations keep their meanings. The double parentheses are relation syntax, not a function invocation. This decision defines a binary relation expression; it does not silently choose precedence for arbitrary mixed chains or turn a whole relation statement into a node selector for subjects.governs.

The Operator supplied these schema-level examples:

```text
Workflow Run ((IS_EXECUTION_OF)) Workflow
Event Record ((RECORDS)) Workflow Run
Runtime ((EXECUTES)) Workflow Run
```

These expressions connect modeled kinds and do not create actual Runs or records. Their Relation Type definitions and derived-inverse declarations must be authored before source admission; notation alone does not establish that they are already registered. The Runtime in the last expression is the live executor, not the Engineering topic or stored engine Code.

Decision record: [CA-A-1240](../CA-A-1240-SPECIFICATION_PROPOSAL--use-named-relation-notation.md).

## Definition, execution and record connections

```text
Workflow Run ((IS_EXECUTION_OF)) Workflow
Event Record ((RECORDS)) Workflow Run
```

Every Workflow Run executes exactly one Workflow; this binding is stated in prose rather than an undefined suffix on a named relation. Workflow is the reusable definition; Workflow Run is an actual Occurrent; Event Record is its persistent description in Journal. The displayed RECORDS target is one supported case, not a closed range restricting every record to Workflow Run. The inverse views HAS_EXECUTION and IS_RECORDED_BY are proposed in the two Definition Drafts; direct facts are stored once. No actual Run or record is created here.

## Step and Substep call boundaries

A leaf Step calls one Action or one Workflow with parameters. A Step containing Substeps makes no call of its own. A Substep is a leaf that calls one Action with parameters: no Workflow calls and no nested Substeps.

```text
Workflow >{1+} Step
Step >{0+} Substep
Substep >{0} @(Substep)
```

Containment connects a Workflow to its Steps and a Step to its Substeps. It does not mean the caller contains the called Workflow or Action definition. No wrapper Action or new execution kind is introduced for Workflow calls.

# Summary

Entity graph candidate with four root branches

## Root decision

Entity is the single root. Every primary graph node and every dependent property is an Entity. Object is narrower: Objects are the abstractions described by the framework, with Continuant and Occurrent specializations. Not every Entity is an Object.

Carrier is a sibling root branch, not a specialization of Object/Continuant. It describes how Objects or their information are represented/stored. A live Occurrent is not stored as the occurrence itself; a persistent record about it can have a Carrier. Do not conflate the occurrence with its record.

# Summary

Design Continuant Occurrent groups and inherited constraints

## Objective

Design a smaller-root Entities Graph candidate with Continuant/Occurrent grouping, inherited common constraints and both derived RMED presentations, using the reviewed Core baseline.

## Details

Child work only; no separately executable own work. The larger review is split into the bounded direct Tasks below before execution.

Required start prerequisite: CA-P-1905. Inputs: its complete pinned inventory and review, the Operator's draft, and current Core definitions.

Group model objects under Continuant and Occurrent. Separate reusable Action/Step/Workflow definitions and Analysis Reports from actual Action/Step/Workflow Runs and analysis activity. Keep a model object's identity separate from its representation.

Use inheritance of common constraints through justified narrower-than specializations. A Plan Atom or Requirement Atom inherits the common Atom Carrier obligation; it does not inherit another Atom's concrete file. Define shared rules once and show subtype additions or differences. Preserve type-specific Status domains and stricter constraints.

Use as few genuine root entities as the evidence permits. Do not invent relations, collapse incompatible identities or force an uncertain classification merely to reduce the count. Report top-level display groups separately from independent model roots and justify each retained root.

Keep Carrier separate from the carried Entity and its binding metadata. Reuse CARRIES/IS_CARRIED_BY rather than invent another equivalent primitive. Carrier-specific fields such as Basename apply only where the relevant Carrier kind supports them.

Deliver both of the latest Operator's views: separate R/M/E/D trees, and an Entity-centered view with applicable M/E/D links. R shows the Entity-model skeleton and required results; M shows construction or Implementation conventions; E shows checks and acceptance criteria; D shows Carrier, representation, format, storage and placement constraints. The two views may share the same source-backed identities and Claims. Do not require an M, E or D Atom for every Entity unless applicable authority requires it.

Treat `/`, `.` and `:` as Entity-model notation, not as automatic Method/Evaluation links. Shared M/E/D Claims may apply to several Entities and need not be copied. A visual M/E/D grouping is not Property ownership, narrower-than inheritance or a newly admitted native Relation. Keep exact applicability and inherited constraints evidenced; unresolved cross-links remain questions. Do not exclude current Carrier definitions merely because their governing source role is Delivery, and do not filter the complete baseline to R-only sources.

Output: a proposed grouped structure, inherited-constraint map, old-to-candidate identity mapping, complete occurrence-to-proposed-relation ledger, comparison of the two RMED view options and explicit questions. This is candidate design, not BFO adoption or Core authority.

The relation ledger must retain **every** old source Subject relation segment, including every `/` occurrence, each supporting qualified prefix and unchanged `:` row. It is not a deduplicated graph-edge list or a ledger only for affected nodes. Each row must record the source Atom ID, Revision and Carrier hash; Subjects field index, complete path and exact segment; original qualified endpoints and graph kind; and disposition with confidence. For an evidenced proposal, record the proposed display operator, canonical Relation and direction, proposed qualified endpoints and evidence span. For an `unresolved` or `not-native` row, leave the asserted native proposal, direction and new endpoints explicitly absent; record the missing-evidence or inapplicability reason, what was checked and any required Operator question. Do not invent a proposal or positive evidence to complete a row.

Classify an old `/` as `/` or `.` only from source Main Content evidence. Propose `@` only where independent Core-declared Carrier-binding evidence supports it, never from Atom incidence or matching spelling. Record aliases and inverse views once as the same underlying Relation, not duplicate facts. Preserve every old occurrence without silent omission, and do not serialize raw `@` into Atom Subjects.

Exclusive scope: read baseline and Core definitions; write candidate structure and design evidence only. Do not update the authoritative Subjects or step-1 graph, or silently remove nodes.

## Summary

Migrate Formal Model syntax and Claims

## Objective

Migrate Current Methodology and direct project-local RMED to the reviewed Model: mechanically migrate Subjects first, adopt the prepared Drafts with correct Subjects, complete entity Definitions and simple formal Claims, rebuild the actual Subject graph, then review and correct it.

## Details

### Scope

Use the existing Current Methodology and direct project-local R/M/E/D boundary. Declare exact Scope Units, statuses and IDs/Versions in P2684. Include only necessary governing-configuration alignment for that same source/subject boundary; do not add new Scope Units or expand configuration/tool features. Existing archived versions and unrelated Drafts are not migrated; selected Current updates create normal predecessors.

C/A/P/O content migration, Engine RMED, code, Tools/MCP/runtime, releases and Terms Graph implementation remain separate. [P2637 owns the later Engine RMED migration](CA-P-2637-EPIC--migrate-engine-rmed-atoms.md). Advanced formulas, functions and conditions in [] remain separate proposals and are excluded here.

### Order

**1. Mechanical Subject migration.** Prepare the exact frontier and thin mappings, then migrate subjects.governs before dependencies using the reviewed Model and new simple relation notation. Preserve content; do not gate this pass on a deep Claim review, adoption or complete missing Definitions. Hold only concrete unresolved mappings. This stage changes Subject-path notation only; it does not create native graph facts or apply newly introduced Relation Types to actual endpoints. Actual typed-relation changes wait until their relevant R Definitions are adopted in Stages 2–3. The later Definition-coverage pass therefore does not block this mechanical Subject pass.

- [CA-P-2684 — prepare the frontier and thin mappings](CA-P-2683-EPIC--migrate-formal-model-syntax-and-claims/01-CA-P-2684-TASK--inventory-current-sources-and-reconcile-migration-drafts.md)
- [CA-P-2689 — apply the mechanical Subject migration](CA-P-2683-EPIC--migrate-formal-model-syntax-and-claims/06-CA-P-2689-TASK--migrate-governing-paths-and-apply-the-new-relations.md)

**2. Adopt the reviewed Drafts with correct Subjects.** Reconcile each selected Draft with its actual Current predecessor, correct Governs/dependencies, then adopt it with the normal identity/version/archive treatment. Use the already reviewed packet; its existence is not adoption.

- [CA-P-2685 — reconcile the plain syntax/layout packet](CA-P-2683-EPIC--migrate-formal-model-syntax-and-claims/02-CA-P-2685-TASK--complete-syntax-rmed-and-markdown-property-contracts.md)
- [CA-P-2688 — adopt the selected Drafts](CA-P-2683-EPIC--migrate-formal-model-syntax-and-claims/05-CA-P-2688-TASK--adopt-the-formal-model-foundations.md)
- [CA-P-2690 — align necessary RMED body properties](CA-P-2683-EPIC--migrate-formal-model-syntax-and-claims/07-CA-P-2690-TASK--migrate-rmed-body-sections-to-logical-properties.md)

**3. Complete Definitions and simple formal Claims.** Build coverage from both the Model and real governing Rs. Reuse existing Definitions before creating missing ones. Every declared in-scope entity must have adopted R/Entity Definition authority; define required properties, cardinalities, basic Formats and Relations. Add faithful R-only formal parts where possible and keep remaining conditions in prose. Preserve meanings and repair consumers before retiring superseded sources.

- [CA-P-2691 — own entity Definition coverage and bounded formalization](CA-P-2683-EPIC--migrate-formal-model-syntax-and-claims/08-CA-P-2691-TASK--formalize-in-scope-claims-in-bounded-batches.md)
- [CA-P-2686 — complete used value Formats](CA-P-2683-EPIC--migrate-formal-model-syntax-and-claims/03-CA-P-2686-TASK--complete-value-format-definitions-and-constraints.md)
- [CA-P-2687 — complete Relation Definitions](CA-P-2683-EPIC--migrate-formal-model-syntax-and-claims/04-CA-P-2687-TASK--define-new-relations-and-their-derived-inverses.md)
- [CA-P-2692 — retire superseded sources after preservation](CA-P-2683-EPIC--migrate-formal-model-syntax-and-claims/09-CA-P-2692-TASK--retire-superseded-contracts-after-preserving-their-meanings.md)

**4. Rebuild the Subject graph.** Generate the selected views from the adopted Current sources, including source IDs/Versions and defining R IDs. Do not substitute the proposal tree or hide unresolved source rows.

**5. Review the rebuilt graph and its Definitions.** Resolve findings, apply the corrections, rebuild and recheck the affected parts. A successful generation alone is not closure.

- [CA-P-2693 — own rebuild, actual-source review and closure](CA-P-2683-EPIC--migrate-formal-model-syntax-and-claims/10-CA-P-2693-TASK--rebuild-the-actual-formal-model-views-and-close-the-migration.md)

### Model and authoring rules

The single root is Entity. Its four sibling branches are Object, Aspect, Graph Syntax and Carrier. Continuant and Occurrent specialize Object; Carrier stays separate from Object. Format and Relation are under Graph Syntax. Follow the latest Operator decisions and the repaired plain packet, not older candidate wording.

Use /, //, ., :, >, existing-kind @ references and ((RELATION_TYPE)); the new model needs no :: branch membership. Only specialization supplies inheritance. Containment has its declared immediate-whole rule; named-relation counts remain in prose. Direct facts are authored once and inverse views derived. A defining Atom can introduce its governed target; a string-format check does not demand prior existence.

Every complete RMED Atom requires direct prose Claim. R alone may add optional content.claim.formal_claim; it does not satisfy the prose count. Operative definitions belong in Claim; Semantics and Details explain/support. The top-level body properties are sibling ## Summary, optional ## Claim scope, ## Claim, optional ## Semantics and ## Details; ### Formal claim nests under Claim.

Use basic [format] and settled cardinalities {n}, {n+}, {n..m}. Counts apply independently to direct values, never nested keys; explicit {0} permits a grouping property with declared children, while omitted cardinality is undefined. list/map are carrier structures and identifying values use string, not ref. YAML null and empty strings are values; Formats and prose decide admissibility. Numeric conditions stay in prose for this scope.

### Tracking and execution

Keep the existing thin [Governs](CA-P-2683-EPIC--migrate-formal-model-syntax-and-claims/governs.tsv) and [Depends On](CA-P-2683-EPIC--migrate-formal-model-syntax-and-claims/depends_on.tsv) tables: Atom ID | old Subject | new Subject | status. Add a thin Definition-coverage list when Stage 3 starts: Subject | defining R IDs/Versions | status. Do not create copied-Claim inventories, per-Atom Analysis reports, confirmations or a new security/history framework.

Use bounded batches and leaf subtasks of at most 15 minutes. Use subagents for independent source/definition lanes with exclusive files. One owner handles shared Journal, adoption and integration. Use the supported operation path, or the already-authorized direct-file route when MCP cannot support it. Do not fix tools in this methodology Epic.

Preserve an existing Atom identity under the applicable rules; Summary or Content Role changes create successor identities. Check only the latest 48 hours of Operator input when confidence is below 90%; the latest words override older ones. If uncertainty remains, choose the best-supported option, create a C/Question, track it in A1305 with the latest candidate, and continue. No new kind, policy, scope boundary, field or function is invented merely to make a source pass.

### Preparation already completed

The [latest Entity-root candidate](../02_analysis/draft/CA-A-1302@1-draft-SPECIFICATION_PROPOSAL--entity-graph-candidate-with-four-root-branches.md) supersedes the root/Type naming of the [prior detailed inventory](../02_analysis/draft/CA-A-1239@1-draft-SPECIFICATION_PROPOSAL--formal-model-primary-kinds-and-properties.md). The prior inventory and selected Drafts were reviewed and repaired. [A1301](../02_analysis/CA-A-1301-ANALYSIS_REPORT--close-the-plain-model-review-repairs.md) closes the ten bounded plain-review findings. [A1297](../02_analysis/done/CA-A-1297-SPECIFICATION_PROPOSAL--separate-advanced-expressions-from-the-plain-model-review.md) defines the advanced-expression exclusion. These are preparation evidence, not Current migration results.

## Definition of Done

The selected Current frontier has migrated Subjects; the selected reviewed Drafts and missing R Definitions are adopted with correct Subjects; every declared in-scope entity has defining R authority; required simple property/Format/cardinality/Relation meaning is complete and advanced expressions stay separate. Superseded sources have a safe meaning/consumer disposition. The actual-source Subject graph has been rebuilt, reviewed, corrected and rechecked. No required unmapped row, missing Definition, broken consumer or omitted source is hidden by Done.

## Progress

Stages 1–3 are complete. The frozen authoring frontier has 1,108 Current Methodology and direct project-local RMED Atoms. Subjects are rooted at Entity; the formerly held Graph Rule paths have been mapped or retired. Forty-eight selected reviewed Drafts were adopted; additional missing Definitions, schemas and canonical legacy retentions were completed through the same staged predecessor-preserving route.

The actual-source coverage has 410 targets and 31 named Relation Types, with no required Definition/format/cardinality gaps. The direct source readback and native-reference checks pass. See [source review](CA-P-2683-EPIC--migrate-formal-model-syntax-and-claims/source-review.md) and [thin Definition coverage](CA-P-2683-EPIC--migrate-formal-model-syntax-and-claims/definition-coverage.tsv). A1305 tracks every chosen Question with the latest candidate.

Stages 4–5 are complete. CA-PROJ-014, CA-PROJ-015 and CA-PROJ-016 publish the primary-kind, property/inheritance and named Relation Type views from the frozen source vector. Actual source and artifact readback, renderer regression checks and bounded independent review pass. All ten child Tasks are Done. See the source-review report for exact evidence and limitations. No Engine, code, runtime, release or deferred Terms/advanced-expression work is included.

## Completion evidence

- [Subject Graph Primary Subjects](../_projection/CA-PROJ-014-CAPRMEDIO--Subject-Graph-Primary-Subjects--Current-Methodology-and-Project-RMED.md)
- [Subject Graph Properties](../_projection/CA-PROJ-015-CAPRMEDIO--Subject-Graph-Properties--Current-Methodology-and-Project-RMED.md)
- [Subject Graph Instances](../_projection/CA-PROJ-016-CAPRMEDIO--Subject-Graph-Instances--Current-Methodology-and-Project-RMED.md)

The model migration is complete for its declared authoring boundary. A1305 retains the chosen continuation Questions; C617 explicitly hands concrete Scope Unit ID carrier encoding to the separate Engine work. Runtime consumers have not been migrated or released by this Epic.

# Summary

Subject graph FPF refinement

## Objective

Resolve the Subject Graph content review with the Operator, one question at a
time. Turn accepted decisions into bounded child Tasks, then correct the source
Atoms and rebuild the affected Subject views.

## Details

### Starting point

The FPF alignment audit of 2026-10-26 found eight open issues in the Current
RMEDO Subject Graph and its governing sources. The reviewed projection is
[CA-PROJ-009](../../_projection/CA-PROJ-009-CAPRMEDIO--Subject-Graph--Current-RMEDO.md),
recorded rebuild 2026-10-26 02:53:08 +0400, with 2,238 sources.

The audit inspected selected source bodies, not every source body. Its findings
and suggested repairs are not approved model changes. Current sources must be
read again before a Task changes them. Latest explicit Operator decisions win.

### Findings to resolve

D01–D08 supplied the accepted repair authority. The original no-Claim and
parallel-derivation-class proposals were rejected by later Operator decisions;
they were not implemented. Optional new design improvements remain proposals.

### Decision process

1. Ask one question with the conflicting source meanings, a proposed resolution,
   and its blast radius. Start with I01, because it affects every later mapping.
2. Record the Operator's answer here. Do not ask again where the latest answer
   already resolves a later issue.
3. Create child Task Atoms from accepted decisions. Each has a bounded source
   set, preserved obligations, dependencies and a checkable completion condition.
   Split own work into at most 15-minute Tasks where practical.
4. Track each issue as decided, tasked, applied and verified. A decision or
   Draft alone is not an applied correction.
5. After the accepted source corrections, rebuild affected views and check the
   specific findings and affected neighbors. Do not restart a general audit.

### Open questions and evidence gaps

- Q01 / G01: Subject/link distinction decided below; implementation tracked by
  P2640, applied and independently verified.
- Q02 / I01: decided by D02. Continuant, Occurrent and Aspect are permitted,
  and the category list is open. P2641 records applied and independently verified source alignment.
- Q03 / I03 and Q04: resolved for this refinement by D04. Every RMED Atom has
  a logical Claim; its representation is not fixed universally. Formal Claims
  may be carried by an Atom or Governing Configuration. No forced conversion
  or test based on the presence of a Semantics section is authorized.
- Q05 / G02: resolved by D05. Standalone archival preserves the existing
  Version; do not create a new Version merely to archive it. P2644 tracks
  alignment with the already-agreed update-predecessor behavior.
- Q06 / I06: resolved by D06/D07. Use explicit derivation between Relation
  Types and retire the old Relation Derivation Class definition. P2645/P2646
  track the accepted work. The prior typed-only decision already supplies the
  direction for related_to; do not ask for that policy again. P2648 tracks its
  bounded retirement and Current consumer correction.
- Q07 / I08: resolved by D08. Actor, Operator and AI Agent definitions belong
  in R, not O. P2647 tracks the source disposition and O catalogue correction.
- I02/I04/I05: the existing decisions already settle the direction: D governs
  the represented thing/property, paths use the accepted canonical root and
  operators, and retired generic fields are not revived. P2649–P2651 perform

- G03: bounded consumer lookup and source correction are complete for the
  accepted repair. Global semantic coverage remains unclaimed: 137 proposals
  were not authored and 69 pre-existing unmapped Subject occurrences remain.
- I10–I12 / F10–F12: optional design-challenge opportunities concern one

### Accepted decisions

D01 — Subject definition, accepted and clarified 2026-10-26:

Subject names the thing or topic an Atom governs or depends on.

That sentence is the definition. GOVERNS / DEPENDS_ON are connected relations,
not part of the Subject definition. Define those relations in separate Atoms
that depend_on the Subject-definition Atom. The whole set of Subjects forms
another graph; those special relations connect Atoms to its nodes.

D02 — Open Graph Node categories, accepted 2026-10-26:

A Graph Node can be Continuant, Occurrent or Aspect. This list is open under
the framework's expandability principle; it is not an exhaustive three-value
enumeration. Do not force every Subject into Continuant or Occurrent, invent
new categories for existing topics, or remap all topics under a new Aspect
path merely from this decision.

D03 — Graph Rule Claim, accepted 2026-10-26:

Graph Rules have a Claim, carried in the YAML part. Absence of a Markdown
Claim section does not mean the logical Claim is absent. This supersedes the
review's proposed no-Claim inheritance exception. D04 below supplies the accepted representation choices; no migration of
existing formal rules into configuration is authorized. Do not silently
duplicate the same operative rule in both forms.

D04 — Claim meaning and representation, accepted 2026-10-26:

- Each RMED Atom has a Claim. State this without defining a universal storage
  location for Claim. This decision does not require a Claim on C, A, P or O.
- A natural-language Claim carries non-formal meaning and uses
  `atom.content.claim`.
- A fully formal Claim (statement) may use structured `atom.claim.*` fields
  or Governing Configuration. Project Structure is an existing precedent for
  the configuration form; do not prescribe it universally for formal Claims.
- YAML that merely contains natural-language prose is not made formal by its
  carrier. Formality is about the statement, not the file extension or an
  optional Semantics section.
- Correct the old no-Claim Graph Rule definitions rather than adding an
  inheritance exclusion. Do not duplicate a formal Claim into Markdown just
  to satisfy an old required-heading rule.

D05 — Standalone archival preserves Version, accepted 2026-10-26:

Archive the existing version without creating another version merely to
archive it. For example, Current CA-R-123 at Version 3 becomes the Archived
representation CA-R-123@3, not a newly invented Version 4. This also agrees
with preserving an update predecessor's historical Version. It does not
prevent a real content update from creating its normal successor Version.
The representation still receives its agreed Archived Status, qualified
identity/filename and archive location. This answer settles the Version
question; do not invent a new timestamp policy from it.

D06 — Derivation between Relation Types, accepted 2026-10-26:

Use the relation "is derived relation of" between Relation Type instances:

CONTAINS — is derived relation of → IS_CONTAINED_BY.

For this known pair, derivation is the inverse with reversed endpoints; the
current R1368 already describes that meaning. This is distinct from an actual
Task/Epic containment link. Preserve direct-only storage of actual links and
inverse derivation. Do not add mandatory derivation-evidence classifications,
new inference behavior or a general transformation engine from this decision.
The precise serialized spelling is not newly chosen here; reuse an admitted
kind if present, otherwise define it under the accepted relation model.

D07 — Retire Relation Derivation Class, accepted 2026-10-26:

Retire the old Relation Derivation Class definition rather than maintain a
parallel classification alongside explicit derivation relations and source
references. Preserve useful source references and the concrete containment
inverse meaning. Do not replace the retired classification with another
mandatory evidence taxonomy or silently remove unrelated obligations.
Coordinate the definition's affected consumers with P2645.

D08 — Actor definitions belong in R, accepted 2026-10-26:

Move the relevant Actor definitions to Requirements, including Operator and
AI Agent definitions. Actor is not an Operations Type. Preserve definitions
already in R; classify actual definitions as R/Type: Definition. A change of
Content Role creates a new Atom ID under the established identity rule;
archive predecessors and account for affected Current consumers. Preserve
participation/authorization constraints when retiring the O/Actor model;
place those normative rules in R rather than silently deleting them.
This is not permission to move every M/E/D that merely mentions an Actor.

Previously established decisions applied to the other findings:

- D Atoms govern the thing/property being represented; representation is in
  their Claim/Content Scope, not an invented Carrier subtype for each field.
- Use full canonical Subject paths and the accepted meanings of /, . and :.
  Repair retired root addresses without redesigning the operative condition.
- Atom.Property and generic Atom.Substance were retired. Do not revive them
  as nodes; use the actual governed thing/property and the accepted Claim

- Relations must have precise typed meanings. Retire the imprecise related_to
  fallback; keep only evidenced typed replacements and drop redundant links,
  rather than inventing dependencies. The child_of/parent_of Epic stays separate.

### Accepted upper-hierarchy alignment follow-through

This continuation follows the original P2640–P2655 milestone above. Its older
source counts, unresolved occurrences and optional proposals describe that
historical milestone; the following records supersede them for this repair.

#### Accepted decisions

- Relation Types have no Status or owning graph. Their canonical names are
  shared and unique within the Project; meaning comes from governing R Claims.
  Relevant inverse, derivation and transitivity semantics are optional.
  Applicable Graph Rules carry constraints. There is no new exact-one defining
  Atom requirement, mandatory admission record, or default admission policy.
- Actions remain separate reusable definitions. A leaf Step or substep launches
  one Action with parameters. A containing Step launches no Action itself.
  Linear Steps have ordered nonconditional substeps. A Conditional Step selects
  one branch and may use Actor input; ON_RESULT is retired.
- Plan decomposition uses child-owned IS_CONTAINED_BY and derived CONTAINS.
  Specialized decomposition relations are retired. For a Plan container becoming
  Done or Canceled, every contained Plan must be Done or Canceled. Mixed terminal
  statuses are allowed. Preserve terminal children and cancel unfinished children
  through the existing cascade. Own work and DoD fulfillment apply to Done,
  not merely to Canceled. Canceled child work is not falsely described as done.
- x:y expresses variable x and ALLOWED value y structurally; it is not an instance
  assignment. Readable kind qualifications remain; // identifies named instances.
  Type is optional for Graph Nodes generally, with specific rules allowed to
  require it. Formal Graph Rule Claims use frontmatter claim.*.
- The framework itself is the reference. No separate example set, authoring
  trial, or mandatory category-admission process is added.

# Summary

Subject graph FPF refinement

## Objective

Resolve the Subject Graph content review with the Operator, one question at a
time. Turn accepted decisions into bounded child Tasks, then correct the source
Atoms and rebuild the affected Subject views.

## Details

### Starting point

The FPF alignment audit of 2026-10-26 found eight open issues in the Current
RMEDO Subject Graph and its governing sources. The reviewed projection is
[CA-PROJ-009](../../_projection/CA-PROJ-009-CAPRMEDIO--Subject-Graph--Current-RMEDO.md),
recorded rebuild 2026-10-26 02:53:08 +0400, with 2,238 sources.

The audit inspected selected source bodies, not every source body. Its findings
and suggested repairs are not approved model changes. Current sources must be
read again before a Task changes them. Latest explicit Operator decisions win.

### Findings to resolve

| ID | Issue and source leads | State |

| I01 | R1994@8 limits Graph Nodes to Continuant/Occurrent, while R2006@7 admits abstract topics. R1275@24 defines Subject as the link rather than its target. | Applied; source checks PASS; bounded FPF alignment PASS |

### Decision process

1. Ask one question with the conflicting source meanings, a proposed resolution,
   and its blast radius. Start with I01, because it affects every later mapping.
2. Record the Operator's answer here. Do not ask again where the latest answer
   already resolves a later issue.
3. Create child Task Atoms from accepted decisions. Each has a bounded source

   Split own work into at most 15-minute Tasks where practical.
4. Track each issue as decided, tasked, applied and verified. A decision or

5. After the accepted source corrections, rebuild affected views and check the
   specific findings and affected neighbors. Do not restart a general audit.
