### Accepted decisions

D01 — Subject definition, accepted and clarified 2026-10-26:

Subject names the thing or topic an Atom governs or depends on.

That sentence is the definition. GOVERNS / DEPENDS_ON are connected relations,
not part of the Subject definition. Define those relations in separate Atoms
that depend_on the Subject-definition Atom. The whole set of Subjects forms
another graph; those special relations connect Atoms to its nodes.

D02 — Open Graph Node categories, accepted 2026-10-26:

A Graph Node can be Continuant, Occurrent or Aspect. This list is open under
the framework's expandability principle; it is not an exhaustive three-value
enumeration. Do not force every Subject into Continuant or Occurrent, invent
new categories for existing topics, or remap all topics under a new Aspect
path merely from this decision.

D03 — Graph Rule Claim, accepted 2026-10-26:

Graph Rules have a Claim, carried in the YAML part. Absence of a Markdown
Claim section does not mean the logical Claim is absent. This supersedes the
review's proposed no-Claim inheritance exception. D04 below supplies the accepted representation choices; no migration of
existing formal rules into configuration is authorized. Do not silently
duplicate the same operative rule in both forms.

D04 — Claim meaning and representation, accepted 2026-10-26:

- Each RMED Atom has a Claim. State this without defining a universal storage
  location for Claim. This decision does not require a Claim on C, A, P or O.
- A natural-language Claim carries non-formal meaning and uses
  `atom.content.claim`.
- A fully formal Claim (statement) may use structured `atom.claim.*` fields
  or Governing Configuration. Project Structure is an existing precedent for
  the configuration form; do not prescribe it universally for formal Claims.
- YAML that merely contains natural-language prose is not made formal by its
  carrier. Formality is about the statement, not the file extension or an
  optional Semantics section.
- Correct the old no-Claim Graph Rule definitions rather than adding an
  inheritance exclusion. Do not duplicate a formal Claim into Markdown just
  to satisfy an old required-heading rule.

D05 — Standalone archival preserves Version, accepted 2026-10-26:

Archive the existing version without creating another version merely to
archive it. For example, Current CA-R-123 at Version 3 becomes the Archived
representation CA-R-123@3, not a newly invented Version 4. This also agrees
with preserving an update predecessor's historical Version. It does not
prevent a real content update from creating its normal successor Version.
The representation still receives its agreed Archived Status, qualified
identity/filename and archive location. This answer settles the Version
question; do not invent a new timestamp policy from it.

D06 — Derivation between Relation Types, accepted 2026-10-26:

Use the relation "is derived relation of" between Relation Type instances:

CONTAINS — is derived relation of → IS_CONTAINED_BY.

For this known pair, derivation is the inverse with reversed endpoints; the
current R1368 already describes that meaning. This is distinct from an actual
Task/Epic containment link. Preserve direct-only storage of actual links and
inverse derivation. Do not add mandatory derivation-evidence classifications,
new inference behavior or a general transformation engine from this decision.
The precise serialized spelling is not newly chosen here; reuse an admitted
kind if present, otherwise define it under the accepted relation model.

D07 — Retire Relation Derivation Class, accepted 2026-10-26:

Retire the old Relation Derivation Class definition rather than maintain a
parallel classification alongside explicit derivation relations and source
references. Preserve useful source references and the concrete containment
inverse meaning. Do not replace the retired classification with another
mandatory evidence taxonomy or silently remove unrelated obligations.
Coordinate the definition's affected consumers with P2645.

D08 — Actor definitions belong in R, accepted 2026-10-26:

Move the relevant Actor definitions to Requirements, including Operator and
AI Agent definitions. Actor is not an Operations Type. Preserve definitions
already in R; classify actual definitions as R/Type: Definition. A change of
Content Role creates a new Atom ID under the established identity rule;
archive predecessors and account for affected Current consumers. Preserve
participation/authorization constraints when retiring the O/Actor model;
place those normative rules in R rather than silently deleting them.
This is not permission to move every M/E/D that merely mentions an Actor.

Previously established decisions applied to the other findings:

- D Atoms govern the thing/property being represented; representation is in
  their Claim/Content Scope, not an invented Carrier subtype for each field.

## Summary

Query Atoms through a synchronized DuckDB Projection

## Proposal

Read governed source files directly, parse their complete YAML Header and Markdown Content with the Current model, and load the result into an in-memory DuckDB database. WORKBENCH provides synchronous native SQL and DuckPGQ graph queries through MCP and a simple web page.

```text
Current model parser ──┬─> atoms
                       ├─> scope_units (Current Scope Unit Declarations only)
                       └─> in-memory DuckDB + DuckPGQ ──> MCP / web
```

Files remain the source of truth. Keep exactly two public tables: `atoms` and `scope_units`. Store no database file, source bytes, raw frontmatter, generated schema artifact, snapshot, cache, or temporary spill file. Source bytes may exist only as transient parser input.

## Sources and model parsing

- Include Current Atoms and Drafts; exclude Archived Atoms. Current means every Current status, including Done and Canceled; Draft rows use their qualified `ID@Version-draft` reference.
- Select canonical Atom carriers from the existing Project inventory. Delivery copies, implementation documentation, and temporary files are not Atom inputs.
- Parse each source directly with the Current model. Do not create a second Declaration-derived schema artifact, generic CFEL evaluator, or prose evaluator. Current Scope Unit Declarations alone define `scope_units`; Draft Declarations are `atoms` rows and do not change Current Scope Unit structure.
- Parse complete YAML Headers and Markdown heading paths. Retain nested Header mappings and native distinctions between missing, null, empty, scalar, list, map, false, and zero. Reject duplicate YAML keys and ambiguous normalized sibling Property names.
- Retain the original Markdown body and complete mapped section occurrences. A `property_path` is a non-empty array of heading segments, not a dotted string. Preserve `heading`, `heading_level`, one-based occurrence `position`, `direct_markdown`, and complete `section_markdown`; the latter includes the heading and full subtree, while the former excludes child Properties. Skipped heading levels create no synthetic segments and fenced heading-like text creates no section. No separate parent-path field is stored.
- Keep direct values separate from descendant subtrees, including the RMED Claim container with Formal Claim and Prose Claim children. Applicable Current Declaration changes that govern scope or Relations refresh the actual indexed facts.

## Materialized relations and hashes

Store only direct Relations found in source files. Materialize declared derived Relations in memory from those direct facts and applicable Current Declarations. Do not infer relations from prose or invent undeclared transitivity.

Each indexed object row carries its outgoing direct and declared-derived Relations. A Task row carries `IS_CONTAINED_BY Epic`; the Epic row carries the derived `CONTAINS Task`. Refresh affected rows, unchanged counterpart objects, their hashes, and the DuckPGQ graph after source or applicable Declaration changes. Remove derived facts when their supporting source fact disappears. A declared inverse is not synthesized twice. Traversal reads materialized facts and does not create a second inverse. Refreshing derived rows does not edit source Atoms or increment their Versions.

Each `atoms` and `scope_units` row carries `hash`: SHA-256 of deterministic canonical row JSON with `hash` excluded, including the entire row after materialized Relation facts are present. Hashes are derived indexed data, not new source Properties. Do not automatically add a hash to arbitrary SQL result rows such as `SELECT COUNT(*)`.

## Queries and interfaces

Use native DuckDB SQL, including CTEs, subqueries, joins, aggregation, sorting, strings, regular expressions, and nested JSON operations. Use the image-bundled DuckPGQ extension for native SQL/PGQ graph queries with `GRAPH_TABLE` and `MATCH`. It queries an in-memory property graph over vertex and edge mappings derived from the two public tables. Do not build a CAPRMEDIO traversal engine or require a custom `expand()` API.

Reachability queries retain the existing requirement: include the unambiguous seed and each reachable typed reference once, follow selected registered Relation Types and directions, and terminate cycles. SQL retrieves objects through joins or subqueries. Current Atoms use base ID references; Drafts use `ID@Version-draft`; Scope Units use names. Preserve both kind and reference in graph identity.

The Trusted SQL MVP admits exactly one native `SELECT` and executes it inside a native `BEGIN TRANSACTION READ ONLY` boundary. External access is disabled and the relevant configuration is locked for public requests. The implementation must not spill to disk and does not use a file-based read-only connection switch. Native statement parsing admits the request; no homemade SQL parser, generic permission layer, or capability-sandbox promise is added.

DuckPGQ internal management calls are unsupported for public requests. An unsupported call may invalidate the connection even under the read-only transaction. Return an explicit engine error stating that restart is required; do not automatically retry the query. An ordinary SQL error leaves the connection usable for the next request.

Run and Check execute synchronously in the originating MCP or web request. MCP Run and Check return complete, untruncated result rows, ordered column names/types, exact row and column counts, and query errors. If the MCP transport cannot carry complete data, return an explicit transport failure rather than silently truncating. The web page has a SQL text area, Run and Check, counts, ordinary result rows, and query errors through the same connector; this proposal does not require all web rows to be materialized or displayed at once and does not define a UI truncation or pagination policy.

## Runtime and refresh

Bundle DuckDB `2.0.0` and the image-bundled DuckPGQ extension in the WORKBENCH Docker image. Trusted startup loads the pair, enables its native SQL/PGQ grammar, builds the in-memory graph, and accepts public queries only after a committed state exists. It does not download dependencies at runtime. Use the existing application, one in-memory database owner per Project, and one technical indexer; Run and Check remain synchronous and need no query jobs, tickets, queues, planner, scheduler, orchestrator, or Workflow/Step wrappers.

Load the selected Current/Draft inventory on startup and reconcile it as the actual inventory changes. Publish source rows, materialized outgoing Relations, row hashes, and graph mappings together so queries cannot see mismatched table and graph state. Cover creates, edits, moves, renames, confirmed removals, and applicable Current Declaration changes. Ordinary internal cache updates are runtime maintenance, not logical Projection mutations.

If a file is invalid, unreadable, or unstable during capture, exclude its indexed values, report the path and error to stderr, and continue with valid inputs. Do not keep stale values, repair the file, or queue an automatic retry. A later actual source change is new input. Source files remain unchanged.

A database or graph update failure publishes no partial state or successful result. Report it to stderr and its caller. Query errors return to the requesting MCP or web caller. Technical query/index activity uses Docker stdout/stderr; this MVP creates no Business Journal record.

## Dependency admission

The minimal Delivery dependency admission is the existing PyYAML parser, `markdown-it-py==4.2.0` for CommonMark heading parsing from the official PyPI packages on Python `>=3.10`, and DuckDB `2.0.0` with image-bundled DuckPGQ. Pin package versions without file hashes. Do not add generic schema-validation or permission-layer dependencies.

## Acceptance and limits

The focused Evaluation Atoms cover Current/Draft membership, complete YAML and Markdown heading-path parsing, native value distinctions, Current Scope Unit Declaration structure, direct and materialized Relation refresh, per-row hashes, synchronous MCP/web behavior, one native SELECT in a read-only transaction, locked external access, no intermediate files or spilling, ordinary versus connection-invalidating engine errors, atomic indexing, and stderr/no-retry source failures.

No runtime implementation or release is claimed by this proposal. Interactive editing, custom result views, renderer behavior, arbitrary CFEL evaluation, generic prose evaluation, and query orchestration remain future work.

## Sources

- [DuckDB graph queries and SQL/PGQ](https://duckdb.org/docs/2.0/guides/sql_features/graph_queries)
- [DuckPGQ extension and supported versions](https://duckdb.org/community_extensions/extensions/duckpgq)
- [PyYAML on PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/PyYAML/)
- [markdown-it-py 4.2.0 on PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/markdown-it-py/4.2.0/)

DuckPGQ is a community extension under active development. These sources establish the selected mechanisms and package publication, not acceptance evidence for this implementation. The selected runtime pair still needs its graph-refresh, trusted-query, connection-error, and no-spill checks.

Store only direct Relations found in source files. Materialize declared derived Relations in memory from those direct facts and applicable Current Declarations. Do not infer relations from prose or invent undeclared transitivity.

Each indexed object row carries its outgoing direct and declared-derived Relations. A Task row carries `IS_CONTAINED_BY Epic`; the Epic row carries the derived `CONTAINS Task`. Refresh affected rows, unchanged counterpart objects, their hashes, and the DuckPGQ graph after source or applicable Declaration changes. Remove derived facts when their supporting source fact disappears. A declared inverse is not synthesized twice. Traversal reads materialized facts and does not create a second inverse. Refreshing derived rows does not edit source Atoms or increment their Versions.

Each `atoms` and `scope_units` row carries `hash`: SHA-256 of deterministic canonical row JSON with `hash` excluded, including the entire row after materialized Relation facts are present. Hashes are derived indexed data, not new source Properties. Do not automatically add a hash to arbitrary SQL result rows such as `SELECT COUNT(*)`.

## Queries and interfaces

Use native DuckDB SQL, including CTEs, subqueries, joins, aggregation, sorting, strings, regular expressions, and nested JSON operations. Use the image-bundled DuckPGQ extension for native SQL/PGQ graph queries with `GRAPH_TABLE` and `MATCH`. It queries an in-memory property graph over vertex and edge mappings derived from the two public tables. Do not build a CAPRMEDIO traversal engine or require a custom `expand()` API.

Reachability queries retain the existing requirement: include the unambiguous seed and each reachable typed reference once, follow selected registered Relation Types and directions, and terminate cycles. SQL retrieves objects through joins or subqueries. Current Atoms use base ID references; Drafts use `ID@Version-draft`; Scope Units use names. Preserve both kind and reference in graph identity.

The Trusted SQL MVP admits exactly one native `SELECT` and executes it inside a native `BEGIN TRANSACTION READ ONLY` boundary. External access is disabled and the relevant configuration is locked for public requests. The implementation must not spill to disk and does not use a file-based read-only connection switch. Native statement parsing admits the request; no homemade SQL parser, generic permission layer, or capability-sandbox promise is added.

DuckPGQ internal management calls are unsupported for public requests. An unsupported call may invalidate the connection even under the read-only transaction. Return an explicit engine error stating that restart is required; do not automatically retry the query. An ordinary SQL error leaves the connection usable for the next request.

Run and Check execute synchronously in the originating MCP or web request. MCP Run and Check return complete, untruncated result rows, ordered column names/types, exact row and column counts, and query errors. If the MCP transport cannot carry complete data, return an explicit transport failure rather than silently truncating. The web page has a SQL text area, Run and Check, counts, ordinary result rows, and query errors through the same connector; this proposal does not require all web rows to be materialized or displayed at once and does not define a UI truncation or pagination policy.

## Runtime and refresh

Bundle DuckDB `2.0.0` and the image-bundled DuckPGQ extension in the WORKBENCH Docker image. Trusted startup loads the pair, enables its native SQL/PGQ grammar, builds the in-memory graph, and accepts public queries only after a committed state exists. It does not download dependencies at runtime. Use the existing application, one in-memory database owner per Project, and one technical indexer; Run and Check remain synchronous and need no query jobs, tickets, queues, planner, scheduler, orchestrator, or Workflow/Step wrappers.

Load the selected Current/Draft inventory on startup and reconcile it as the actual inventory changes. Publish source rows, materialized outgoing Relations, row hashes, and graph mappings together so queries cannot see mismatched table and graph state. Cover creates, edits, moves, renames, confirmed removals, and applicable Current Declaration changes. Ordinary internal cache updates are runtime maintenance, not logical Projection mutations.

If a file is invalid, unreadable, or unstable during capture, exclude its indexed values, report the path and error to stderr, and continue with valid inputs. Do not keep stale values, repair the file, or queue an automatic retry. A later actual source change is new input. Source files remain unchanged.

A database or graph update failure publishes no partial state or successful result. Report it to stderr and its caller. Query errors return to the requesting MCP or web caller. Technical query/index activity uses Docker stdout/stderr; this MVP creates no Business Journal record.

## Dependency admission

The minimal Delivery dependency admission is the existing PyYAML parser, `markdown-it-py==4.2.0` for CommonMark heading parsing from the official PyPI packages on Python `>=3.10`, and DuckDB `2.0.0` with image-bundled DuckPGQ. Pin package versions without file hashes. Do not add generic schema-validation or permission-layer dependencies.

## Acceptance and limits

The focused Evaluation Atoms cover Current/Draft membership, complete YAML and Markdown heading-path parsing, native value distinctions, Current Scope Unit Declaration structure, direct and materialized Relation refresh, per-row hashes, synchronous MCP/web behavior, one native SELECT in a read-only transaction, locked external access, no intermediate files or spilling, ordinary versus connection-invalidating engine errors, atomic indexing, and stderr/no-retry source failures.

No runtime implementation or release is claimed by this proposal. Interactive editing, custom result views, renderer behavior, arbitrary CFEL evaluation, generic prose evaluation, and query orchestration remain future work.

# Summary

Implement an RMED-guided Engine Workflow

## Objective

Provide a FRAMEWORK_ENGINE implementation Workflow that uses the new Tools to turn selected active RMED authority into tested Implementation, with each Step executed in its own subagent and all unresolved issues reported.

## Details

This is a new Engine Epic, not an extension of the completed release Epic. Author only this Plan and its Tasks now. Implementation, new governing O/RMED, runtime registration and effects happen when its Tasks are executed.

### Runtime flow

1. Gather all active Rs selected for implementation and assess their conflicts and gaps.
2. Compile all applicable active Ms into a derived projection.
3. Compile all applicable E policies into a separate derived projection; retain suitable existing E cases separately.
4. Compile all applicable Ds into a separate derived projection.
5. Review the R/M/E/D inputs together and report conflicts, gaps and ambiguity before affected implementation.
6. Reuse or create E test cases so every selected R has at least one case and all required behaviors are covered.
7. Implement the tests using the Ms, E policies and Ds.
8. Implement the Rs using the Ms and Ds, then run the agreed tests and report actual outcomes.

M/E/D preparation may run in parallel after selection. Each Step runs in a fresh subagent and consumes saved outputs from prior Steps. Each Epic Task is also assigned to its own subagent when executed. No extra reviewer-after-every-Step machinery is required.

### New Tools only

The runtime uses the accepted CONNECTOR_TOOLS query/read/create/modify contract and the receiving TOOL_WORKFLOWS policy boundaries. Explicitly select Active content, the requested scope and any descendant/applicability boundary; connectors do not invent those defaults. No legacy direct mutation/CLI fallback bypasses these boundaries.

New Tool implementation is presently pending. CA-P-2252/2253/2254/2259/2260/2268 and relevant consumer bindings under CA-P-2269–2272 are shared prerequisites, not duplicate work in this Epic. Source contracts or old installed routes do not establish new Tool readiness. Source/prompt preparation may proceed against accepted contracts; affected executable use remains blocked until the required new Tools are implemented and verified.

### Inputs and projections

Inputs identify the target Scope Unit or explicit R set and the implementation boundary. Resolve the declared Scope Unit tree through the new Scope Unit Query/Read bindings (CA-O-211/CA-O-212, implemented by CA-P-2254). Supply the resulting explicit unit frontier to Atom Query; neither folder traversal nor Atom Query derives the tree. Unit-based selection uses Targeting Atoms, or Subtree-targeting Atoms when descendants are selected: resolve Claim Target Scope Unit, with the current Scope Unit default, rather than confuse ownership with applicability. Include eligible parent-owned Goal/Demand Atoms targeting the selected unit and applicable ancestor constraints; keep these sets identified and deduplicate by Atom identity. Collect all applicable active authority, such as TOOLS plus TOOL_NAME and applicable ancestors, without collecting unrelated sibling Tools. Each compiler explicitly Queries identities, then full-Reads every selected Atom through CA-O-047. Preserve the complete operative content, actual current_state/source-view evidence and readable original-source reference/Version. Partial Query results, unreadable sources and incomplete selection do not become complete projections. It remains derived and is never a new source of truth. This Epic does not require a new hash/snapshot/sealing framework.

Projection agents and implementation agents report issues with Rs, Ms, E policies/cases and Ds throughout the Run. Reports identify affected originals, the ambiguity/conflict/gap, impact and any evidence-supported proposal. Blocking issues go to the Operator; the workflow does not silently rewrite authority or pretend incomplete inputs are ready. Changed source inputs require renewed affected preparation.

### Tests and completion

Maintain an R → E case → executable test coverage map. Count only verified current Evaluation cases whose direct evaluation_for relation includes the selected R. New creation must return confirmed identity/state/effects and recorded evidence; proposed, Draft, failed or effect-uncertain cases do not satisfy coverage. Functional/public-interface and focused integration checks are the default emphasis. Useful unit/semantic checks are retained for pure logic, without a fixed test ratio; installed end-to-end checks are used where the narrower boundary cannot expose the important behavior. Reuse current CA-E-389/CA-M-285 policy and suitable existing cases rather than duplicate them.

Tests are implemented before required behavior. Record genuine unmet-behavior baselines separately from broken test harnesses; existing correct behavior may already pass. Final completion requires actual execution of the selected tests, complete Requirement accounting and an honest remaining-issue/effect report. Confidence and permissions come from current applicable settings, Plan/Run inputs and Operator delegation.

CA-P-2292 owns the missing private Engine run-output writer and its supporting delivery contract. It writes the four derived inputs only under .caprmedio_caprmedio/_projection/ENGINE_IMPLEMENTATION/<run_id>/ and the full report at .caprmedio_tmp/ENGINE_IMPLEMENTATION/<run_id>.md, returns verified repository-relative references, and reuses workflow_run_support for shared Run/Step/Action Journal linkage. It does not use Atom Create to store projections, mutate authoritative Atoms or introduce a generic public artifact API. Outputs retain existing Run/Step/subagent identities and input current_state evidence; another Run's output is never overwritten. Do not add automatic release, retry/recovery, whole-project repair, live Subject migration or a new universal Tool family. Necessary missing capabilities are reported or linked to their existing owners.

## Definition of Done

- The O flow and its supporting Engine RMED have been reviewed against this Epic.
- Every Step has short instructions, declared new-Tool bindings and a fresh-subagent input/output contract.
- All selected Rs have linked E cases and implemented tests; prepared inputs preserve all applicable active Ms, E policies and Ds.
- Actual isolated fixtures prove the complete test-first path and truthful conflict, gap, missing-Tool and Implementation-issue reports.
- Workflow discovery/execution, full reports and shared Journal outcomes are verified through the new Tools; no source-only readiness or hidden legacy fallback is claimed.

# Summary

Make Atom and Scope Unit Actions Good

## Objective

Make the PROGRAMMATIC Atom actions complete, coherent and usable through the existing connectors, Workflows and MCP. Scope Unit operations, structure validation/reconciliation and topology mutations are deferred to separate peer Epic CA-P-2480, Make Atom and Scope Unit Actions Good — Stage 2. This Epic records the Operator's decisions from this session; it is not evidence that the implementation already provides them. Its operating-context work now also covers configurable model composition and a shared multi-Project Docker/MCP runtime, with explicit adoption and implementation gates.

## Details

### Agreed PROGRAMMATIC structure

The target structure is:

```text
PROGRAMMATIC
├── TOOLS
│   ├── CONNECTORS
│   └── CAPRMEDIO_TOOLS
├── PROJECT_TOOLS
└── APPS
    ├── WORKFLOW_ORCHESTRATOR
    └── MCP
```

All shown Scope Units are unordered; individual Tool Scope Units belong under the appropriate Tool group.

- TOOLS contains reusable capabilities delivered with the framework, rather than maintenance specific to this repository.
- CONNECTORS contains logical storage access and file/folder mechanics. Backend-specific implementations are adapters within CONNECTORS, not another peer feature group. Connectors do not choose Atom identity, lifecycle or Workflow sequencing.
- CAPRMEDIO_TOOLS contains reusable CAPRMEDIO domain actions, including the Atom and Scope Unit actions in this Epic, usable in any CAPRMEDIO-managed project.
- PROJECT_TOOLS contains only the build, test, release and maintenance operations specific to developing the caprmedio framework repository itself. It is a sibling of TOOLS, not a child of CAPRMEDIO_TOOLS.
- APPS contains WORKFLOW_ORCHESTRATOR and MCP as peers. The orchestrator owns Workflow execution and coordination using Tools. MCP owns discovery and transport for Tools and Workflows; it does not own orchestration or duplicate domain behavior. Preserve other existing Apps; this tree highlights the agreed boundary.

The implementation tasks must reconcile existing TOOLS, CONNECTOR_TOOLS, TOOL_WORKFLOWS, PROJECT_TOOLS, APPS and MCP declarations and contents with this target, reusing capabilities rather than creating duplicate owners. Align applicable RMEDO, project_structure.toml and both governing/delivery bindings during that migration. This Epic update records the target only; it does not itself rename or move folders, change scope declarations, or implement Tools.

### Atom actions

- Find Atoms using filters on any supported Atom property, including nested properties and relations; do not restrict Find to Subjects or a fixed small property whitelist. Validate typed filters and report invalid sources or incomplete coverage rather than silently ignoring them.
- Create any Content Role and applicable Type directly in any status admitted by that Role/Type model, filling and validating all mandatory fields. Do not require intermediate statuses, complete Journal history or retained Draft lineage.
- Update by publishing the next revision file and archiving the exact predecessor. Preserve same identity where current change-classification rules allow it; identity-changing replacement remains distinct. An actual edit advances revision metadata; a no-op does not create a revision or archive.
- Promote ID-free Drafts to Active with a fresh unused identity; no restoration of a previous ID or history/Journal admission gate.
- Cover ordinary file Atoms and folder-backed Plan and Operations containers, including Plan/Epic, Workflow and Step. Preserve exact prior bundles and current container semantics; compose explicitly selected per-Atom operations for bulk work rather than promising a cross-Atom transaction.

Stage 1 consumes existing valid Scope Unit bindings for Atom placement safety; Scope Unit and Project Structure validation/reconciliation belong to Stage 2. # Summary

Make Atom and Scope Unit Actions Good

## Objective

Make the PROGRAMMATIC Atom actions complete, coherent and usable through the existing connectors, Workflows and MCP. Scope Unit operations, structure validation/reconciliation and topology mutations are deferred to separate peer Epic CA-P-2480, Make Atom and Scope Unit Actions Good — Stage 2. This Epic records the Operator's decisions from this session; it is not evidence that the implementation already provides them. Its operating-context work now also covers configurable model composition and a shared multi-Project Docker/MCP runtime, with explicit adoption and implementation gates.

## Details

### Agreed PROGRAMMATIC structure

The target structure is:

```text
PROGRAMMATIC
├── TOOLS
│   ├── CONNECTORS
│   └── CAPRMEDIO_TOOLS
├── PROJECT_TOOLS
└── APPS
    ├── WORKFLOW_ORCHESTRATOR
    └── MCP
```

All shown Scope Units are unordered; individual Tool Scope Units belong under the appropriate Tool group.

- TOOLS contains reusable capabilities delivered with the framework, rather than maintenance specific to this repository.
- CONNECTORS contains logical storage access and file/folder mechanics. Backend-specific implementations are adapters within CONNECTORS, not another peer feature group. Connectors do not choose Atom identity, lifecycle or Workflow sequencing.
- CAPRMEDIO_TOOLS contains reusable CAPRMEDIO domain actions, including the Atom and Scope Unit actions in this Epic, usable in any CAPRMEDIO-managed project.
- PROJECT_TOOLS contains only the build, test, release and maintenance operations specific to developing the caprmedio framework repository itself. It is a sibling of TOOLS, not a child of CAPRMEDIO_TOOLS.
- APPS contains WORKFLOW_ORCHESTRATOR and MCP as peers. The orchestrator owns Workflow execution and coordination using Tools. MCP owns discovery and transport for Tools and Workflows; it does not own orchestration or duplicate domain behavior. Preserve other existing Apps; this tree highlights the agreed boundary.

The implementation tasks must reconcile existing TOOLS, CONNECTOR_TOOLS, TOOL_WORKFLOWS, PROJECT_TOOLS, APPS and MCP declarations and contents with this target, reusing capabilities rather than creating duplicate owners. Align applicable RMEDO, project_structure.toml and both governing/delivery bindings during that migration. This Epic update records the target only; it does not itself rename or move folders, change scope declarations, or implement Tools.

### Atom actions

- Find Atoms using filters on any supported Atom property, including nested properties and relations; do not restrict Find to Subjects or a fixed small property whitelist. Validate typed filters and report invalid sources or incomplete coverage rather than silently ignoring them.
- Create any Content Role and applicable Type directly in any status admitted by that Role/Type model, filling and validating all mandatory fields. Do not require intermediate statuses, complete Journal history or retained Draft lineage.
- Update by publishing the next revision file and archiving the exact predecessor. Preserve same identity where current change-classification rules allow it; identity-changing replacement remains distinct. An actual edit advances revision metadata; a no-op does not create a revision or archive.
- Promote ID-free Drafts to Active with a fresh unused identity; no restoration of a previous ID or history/Journal admission gate.
- Cover ordinary file Atoms and folder-backed Plan and Operations containers, including Plan/Epic, Workflow and Step. Preserve exact prior bundles and current container semantics; compose explicitly selected per-Atom operations for bulk work rather than promising a cross-Atom transaction.

### Scope Unit actions — deferred to Stage 2

CA-P-2480 owns Scope Unit create/rename/move/delete, Project Structure and governing/delivery folder validation/reconciliation, and physical/declaration topology migration. Its first inventory Task CA-P-2483 is Backlog. The empty-only deletion decision remains binding there. Historical completed Scope Unit audits retain their original parent/history and are reused as evidence, not moved or claimed as Stage 2 completion.

### Validation and reconciliation

Validate YAML syntax, applicable Role/Type keys, mandatory properties and typed values; exact Markdown heading set and order; and coherence among carried properties, filename and actual placement. Stage 1 consumes existing valid Scope Unit bindings for Atom placement safety; Scope Unit and Project Structure validation/reconciliation belong to Stage 2. Deferral does not waive normal Atom placement or unsafe-binding refusal.

Validate registered relation/placement invariants. For example, the current task membership of an Epic's folder must equal its declared direct decomposition membership, applying reserved status-directory and current-revision rules. Use the registered direct relation and derive inverses; do not add a second independent child list, infer Workflow control flow from containment, or count archived predecessor files as extra current members.

Separate mismatch detection from repair. Support three explicitly selected reconciliation policies: files/folders canonical (repair properties and applicable relations), properties canonical (repair filenames and folder placement), or manual (report differences and make no repair). Canonical means the selected repair direction for this mismatch, not permission to bypass validation, invent identity/semantics, overwrite collisions or discard content. Ambiguous or unsafe repairs remain visible without effects.

### Shared design

Reuse the current coherent connector interface and existing storage owners. Keep domain rules in one owner and file/folder mechanics in adapters. Provide one logical property-update entry point whose mapping resolves whether a property is carried in YAML or in its named Markdown section; do not duplicate values or bypass lifecycle/revision rules.

Represent supported schema/declaration data in versioned external files rather than scattered hard-coded property/heading rules. Preserve protected Content Role meanings while allowing the admitted Type, Relation Type and Graph Rule extension points. Choose the format explicitly; JSON is a candidate. External data must retain its governing authority and not become an independent conflicting source. Cover property location, mandatory/allowed keys, values and body layout.

# Summary

Prepare a fresh isolated MCP audit image and harness

## Objective

Admit an audit-owned disposable MCP fixture without affecting the production Project MCP, before any scoped failure reproduction.

## Details

This bounded child splits image/harness preparation from the parent safety preflight. Reuse existing current-code test image and Project launcher harnesses; do not implement a new server or change product code. Read the exact protected-root/instance/port/container receipt in .caprmedio_tmp/mcp-audit-20261020/isolation/preflight-receipt.md. Production port56317, production root/state/container/image and every retained previous fixture are excluded from test targets and cleanup.

Prepare one fresh immutable current-source test image under an audit-owned attempt; do not tag over or remove production/existing images. Use a fresh non-symlink strict child of .caprmedio_tmp/mcp-audit-20261020/isolation for project/golden fixtures and separate state/locks/cache/Runs/receipts/Journal. Verify distinct loopback ports, exact root/control-root labels, instance IDs, namespace and mounts before invoking any MCP test. Serialize Docker build/test execution, preserve declared resource caps, and stop with an attributable hold rather than exhausting host resources. No production test traffic, port probe, stop, restart, reload, redeploy or cleanup is permitted. Normal production traffic is not test evidence.

Retain protected-file and normalized production-container pre/post snapshots, exact test commands, immutable image digest, created fixture IDs/paths/ports and any fixture-only cleanup receipts. Existing two-project launcher proof may be used only with fresh fixture identities and no production selection. If readiness or guarded execution is unavailable, retain truthful unverified/blocked state; never substitute production or declare current defect resolution from source tests alone.

### Budget and dependency

Own work at most15minutes; split any longer image/harness attempt into a separately recorded bounded subtask before continuation. Use a Luna worker. Parent: CA-P-2408. The four historical audit lanes need no test endpoint. Current reproductions under CA-P-2409 require this admission and the parent isolation checks.

### Prepared admission and bounded smoke continuation

A fresh audit-only immutable image and fixture admission were prepared under the isolated attempt, with protected pre/post equality. No server or MCP smoke has run. The initial review required no-write interpreter, exact loopback-port projection and immediate source/Compose rechecks; these guards are under independent re-review. [CA-P-2419](01-CA-P-2410-TASK--prepare-a-fresh-isolated-mcp-audit-image-and-harness/01-CA-P-2419-TASK--launch-the-isolated-mcp-fixture-and-verify-context-smoke.md) owns any later bounded fixture launch/smoke only after unconditional guard acceptance. This parent remains Active until those results and production non-interference are verified.

### Definition of Done

A fresh immutable image and disposable fixture endpoint are identity-checked, scoped smoke/admission evidence and production non-interference receipts are retained, and exact supported/blocked limits are stated. No production or existing fixture is changed. Planning checkpoint: not started.

# Summary

Establish explicit Term Definitions and staged CCE consistency checks

## Question

How were the seventeen-RMED CCE packet and its necessary consumers reconciled with the Current subject system and promoted?

## Scope

Source adoption of the original seventeen-RMED packet in CORE_META_MODEL, including the three previously promoted Methods, plus narrow compatibility updates to optional terminology consumers. This Analysis remains a provisional tracking Draft. Runtime, parser, generated-view publication, project-wide vocabulary migration and complete occurrence review are outside these source effects.

## Approach

Apply the Operator's latest decisions over older Draft text. Verify Current authority from Project Structure, rebase stale candidates without losing adopted metadata or formal constraints, independently review the new Subject bindings and semantic boundaries, allocate fresh identities under the canonical Project lock, archive actual Current predecessors and consume only the fourteen remaining packet Drafts. Record actual source effects independently in the Journal.

## Results

### Accepted model

Each reusable Term has one explicit authoritative R/Term Definition. M explains writing its content; E checks well-formedness and consistent use in stages: entity names, Claim, Claim Scope, Semantics, Details and remaining authored fields. D carries content and review evidence through existing carriers. No dictionary Projection or lookup service is a prerequisite.

Complete canonical entity names retain one-to-one bindings and exact authored usage. `atom.id` and `projection.id` are distinct complete qualified property names using the same ID meaning; their terminal component need not be globally unique. ID means a unique identifier used to find an entity instance across Continuant and Occurrent instances, with uniqueness within matching prefix namespaces. The supplied version/state-qualified identifier examples do not independently establish lifecycle equivalence or a general case-folding rule.

`Package` is reused in `Package`, `Eval Package` and `Runtime Package`; `Unit` in `Scope Unit` and `Code Unit`. The chain `Package > Module > Code Unit` connects three entities without a fourth chain entity. Qualification syntax, explicit definitions and source identity remain separate. Ordinary words, property labels, instance labels and path spelling do not automatically become Project Terms or defining authority.

### New subject system and resolved lexical binding

Current authority uses the `Entity` root with Object, Aspect, Graph Syntax and Carrier branches. References use admitted `/`, `//`, `.`, `:`, `>`, existing-kind `@(...)` and named-relation syntax. The old `Subject/CAPRMEDIO/...` paths and unsupported `::` notation were removed from operative packet references. RMED bodies now use Current CA-D-479@25 sibling headings: Summary, optional Claim scope, Claim, optional Semantics and Details; required formal constraints in existing sources were preserved.

**Q-TERM-TARGET is resolved from Current authority.** CA-R-1318 establishes the Term kind; CA-R-2229 establishes the distinct Term Definition Type; CA-R-1194@29 permits a defining Atom to introduce its target; CA-R-1931@15 and CA-R-2002@15 admit named-instance `K//Name` syntax. Accordingly, the explicit ID Term Definition introduces and governs `Entity/Object/Continuant/Term//ID`. That lexical Term object is distinct from Atom or Projection property entities. Parsing property names does not create it, invent Unit/domain objects or implement a Terms Graph. Existing Term placement is not reclassified.

The Type Draft was merged into existing CA-R-2229, not allocated as a duplicate Type. Entity Definition of the Term kind remains distinct from lexical Term Definition ownership; the former does not silently grant Governed Term status to every word in its text.

Establish explicit Term Definitions and staged CCE consistency checks

## Question

Apply the Operator's latest decisions over older Draft text. ### Accepted model

Each reusable Term has one explicit authoritative R/Term Definition. M explains writing its content; E checks well-formedness and consistent use in stages: entity names, Claim, Claim Scope, Semantics, Details and remaining authored fields. D carries content and review evidence through existing carriers. No dictionary Projection or lookup service is a prerequisite.

Complete canonical entity names retain one-to-one bindings and exact authored usage. `atom.id` and `projection.id` are distinct complete qualified property names using the same ID meaning; their terminal component need not be globally unique. ID means a unique identifier used to find an entity instance across Continuant and Occurrent instances, with uniqueness within matching prefix namespaces. The supplied version/state-qualified identifier examples do not independently establish lifecycle equivalence or a general case-folding rule.

Current authority uses the `Entity` root with Object, Aspect, Graph Syntax and Carrier branches. References use admitted `/`, `//`, `.`, `:`, `>`, existing-kind `@(...)` and named-relation syntax. # Summary

Declare the Node branch and derive the graph from Formal Claims

## Question

How should the graph model, Declaration Forms and notation change so that one coherent source declares each Node without repeated inherited definitions or ambiguous constraints?

## Scope

This proposal covers governing Drafts for the Node branch, graph Relations and notation, Role/Form naming, carrier mappings and formal Scope. It records the latest human decisions; earlier conflicting alternatives are superseded. The [Epic successor Draft](../../../../../03_plan/draft/CA-P-2694@39-draft-EPIC--entity-graph-refactor-stage-4-polishing.md) tracks adoption and implementation dependencies.

Actual Workflow, Step, Substep and Action instance review/migration is deferred by the latest Operator instruction. This pass reviews their model declarations and constraints; model-level examples do not perform instance review.

## Approach

Write the governing Drafts directly, keep the design rationale here, and review the packet before adoption. Preserve Current sources and completed publication history. Resolve exact source-to-Node mappings before replacing Definitions; never replace all `/` edges with composition.

## Results

### What changes

- **Carrier placement is explicit.** Use `@Carrier//Markdown file`. Deliver non-Content Objects into frontmatter. Deliver Content descendants into Markdown. Frontmatter is delimited YAML at the beginning of the file. Carrier filename/location are properties; location is repository-relative.
- **Node scope is explicit.** `Node/**, .**` selects narrower entities plus their Properties. Add `Node` when a rule also covers the root.

- **Names and values use separate expressions.** `p{:0..1}: [format]{:1}` separates occurrence from values. `p.*[...]` constrains immediate names. `p.**[...]` constrains names recursively. Expressions use semicolons.
- **Claim is one Property.** Keep `Atom.Content.Claim`. Formal content is an optional CFEL fence inside its Markdown value. No separate Formal Claim Property is retained. RMED Claim is required. Claim Scope, Semantics and Details are optional.
- **Delivery specifies representation.** `>>` delivers Objects to a referenced Carrier or its parts. Object means Node instance. Filename/location formula details remain separate until expressible.

- **Analysis is freeform.** `Atom.Content.**[string]{:0+}: [markdown]{:1}` constrains each dependent Property recursively. Sibling names are unique. `x.y.z` differs from `x.z`. Shared Atom constraints remain inherited.

- **Graph Syntax becomes CFEL — CAPRMEDIO Formal Expression Language.** CFEL covers expression syntax and meaning for Subject addresses and Formal Claims. Graph, CFEL and Carrier remain distinct model components. This names the existing language; it does not add notation.

- **Declaration is a Form of Requirement.** Use `Role: Requirement / Form: Declaration` and the existing R prefix. Within each selected effective MODEL, each declared member selected by `(Node, Node/**, .**)`, including Properties, has one effective Current Declaration with one matching active Subject. Count only those Declarations; other RMED may address the same Node. Use CFEL Formal Claims where possible. Use Claim prose only for constraints CFEL cannot express. Keep brief Semantics for Primary Nodes only. Each Property Declaration specifies two contracts: direct-value format/cardinality; dependent-entity format/cardinality. Unchanged inherited Properties reuse their original Declaration; explicit MODEL overrides select their local replacement. CFEL entities retain a Claim and may have Semantics.
- **Use Role and Form.** Rename Content Role to Role and the Role-specific Type to Form. These names express different purposes. Naming Methods prefer words that convey the actual distinction and reuse canonical expressions consistently; they do not impose a blanket word ban on useful contextual uses of `content`, `entity` or `type`.
- **Use two root kinds.** MODEL and PROJECT STRUCTURE are Primary Node kinds declared in CAPRMEDIO's self-describing MODEL. Their instance roots are `MODEL//CAPRMEDIO`, `PROJECT STRUCTURE//CAPRMEDIO`, and the corresponding consumer Project roots. The consumer MODEL is optional. PROJECT STRUCTURE describes Scope Structure, Aspects and other declared components. Core Meta-Model contains the Atoms defining CAPRMEDIO's MODEL. Extensible axis configuration stays deferred.
- **Declare Scope outside the constrained Unit.** State permitted active/passive Subjects and Relation endpoints/cardinalities. ENGINE's proposed Scope permits allowed instances and implementation RMED; model definitions use their declared model-defining Scope. A local MODEL does not automatically widen ENGINE's Scope. Target Scope never grants wider authority.
- **Keep graph meanings distinct.** `/` narrows Primary Nodes with inheritance, `//` names their instances, `.` addresses Properties, `+>`/`<+` expresses composition, and `>|`/`|<` expresses classification. Composition uses canonical IS_CONTAINED_BY and derived CONTAINS; Container has yes/no value cases. `(Node, Node/**, .**)` includes the root, its recursive narrower branch and their recursive Properties. `@` references an existing target, parentheses group, and `in (...)` states membership. `:` denotes an allowed value, `=` tests, and `==` establishes a required/derived conclusion. In Subjects, `:=` combines allowed value and condition, as in `Atom/(.Role := Method)`. It does not write an instance value or exclude other allowed values from Atom.Role. Formal Claims keep `:` and `=` separate. Full Formal Claims stay out of Subjects; `..` and an invented `::` meaning are excluded.
- **Keep both counts.** Relation cardinality constrains both written directions; reversal swaps the counts. Property syntax uses separate expressions for occurrence, direct values and immediate dependent names: `p{:occurrence count}; p: [value format]{:value count}; p.*[name format]{:child count}`. YAML and Markdown mappings preserve that distinction, including mixed section content and nested headings.
- **Derive Primary Node versus Property.** The Node branch permits zero or one IS_PROPERTY_OF bearer. Zero derives Primary Node and no direct value; one derives Property and forbids narrowing and instantiation. Property-bearing must be acyclic. HAS_VALUE binds a Property on an instance to a literal, such as CA-P-123.version = 1; literals do not become declared graph Nodes.
- **Inheritance supplies effective rules.** Narrower instances receive applicable Relation cardinalities and declared Property constraints. Do not redeclare an inherited Property or create a new Declaration merely for an inherited lookup. Each Node's single effective Declaration in the selected MODEL resolves its Relation whitelist, endpoint constraints and counts. MODEL inheritance may replace any inherited rule through an explicit local override; unchanged Declarations are reused. Inheritance neither copies instance facts nor gives a Property a second bearer.
- **Operations use siblings and explicit composition.** Workflow, Step, Substep and Action narrow Operations. Each Workflow has one or more Steps, each Step one Workflow. A Step exclusively runs one Action or contains one or more Substeps. Each Substep has one Step and runs one Action. Actions may have zero or more callers. RUN bindings do not establish execution evidence.
- **Store authored instance Relations once.** Rename Subject links to active/passive; store modeled authored Node-instance links under `relations`, with typed containment references. Derive HAS_ACTIVE_SUBJECT from the dedicated Subject field and derive inverse views. The exact Assignee/Target reference migration remains open.

Relation Definitions now state allowed Host/Target signatures and reuse `Direct ((HAS_INVERSE)) Derived`. Inverse views have no separate Definition Atom. Repeated migration commentary is removed from the governing Drafts.

### Why these changes

The human rationale is to remove words that add no useful distinction, keep each complete expression precise, and avoid defining inherited material repeatedly. Primary Nodes, Properties, narrowing, composition and classification need different meanings so the graph can express constraints faithfully. A formal Scope outside its Unit makes the Unit's permitted authority explicit. One Declaration gathers a Node's structure and permissions; formal rules support graph reconstruction without turning an address into a second programming language. Syntax explanations remain useful where symbols are not self-explanatory.

### MODEL and PROJECT STRUCTURE — latest architecture

The two kinds are declared in MODEL//CAPRMEDIO itself. The named Subject roots are their instances:

```text
MODEL//CAPRMEDIO
PROJECT STRUCTURE//CAPRMEDIO
    <+ Scope Structure
    <+ Aspects

MODEL//<PROJECT NAME>              (optional)
PROJECT STRUCTURE//<PROJECT NAME>
    <+ Scope Structure
    <+ Aspects
```

The Project name above is a placeholder. A Project uses MODEL//CAPRMEDIO. It may define a local MODEL. A local MODEL inherits MODEL//CAPRMEDIO and may override any inherited rule. No inherited rule requires an overridable marker.

One Current authoritative Declaration per Node means one effective Declaration within the selected MODEL. Unchanged inherited Declarations are reused. A local replacement and its base source can coexist without becoming two effective owners in that MODEL. This selection context is distinct from the Project-wide instance context used by UNIQUE.

Core Meta-Model is a Scope Unit in CAPRMEDIO's Scope Structure. It contains the governing Atoms defining MODEL//CAPRMEDIO, including the two root kinds. This self-description does not identify the MODEL instance with its Scope Unit or PROJECT STRUCTURE instance. Existing ordered Scope Unit proposals remain subject to exact registration and mapping.

Model inheritance connects MODEL instances. It is separate from `/` Node narrowing and `<+` containment. The inheritance Relation name and exact Model-selection/override binding still need specification; this pass adds no invented notation or runtime behavior.

This replaces the earlier owner-wrapper layout and the MODEL-versus-PROJECT root split. The rationale is to distinguish reusable declarations from each Project's actual structure, reuse inherited material, and let each local MODEL control all of its effective rules.

# Summary

Declare the Node branch and derive the graph from Formal Claims

## Question

How should the graph model, Declaration Forms and notation change so that one coherent source declares each Node without repeated inherited definitions or ambiguous constraints?

## Scope

This proposal covers governing Drafts for the Node branch, graph Relations and notation, Role/Form naming, carrier mappings and formal Scope. It records the latest human decisions; earlier conflicting alternatives are superseded. The [Epic successor Draft](../../../../../03_plan/draft/CA-P-2694@39-draft-EPIC--entity-graph-refactor-stage-4-polishing.md) tracks adoption and implementation dependencies.

Actual Workflow, Step, Substep and Action instance review/migration is deferred by the latest Operator instruction. This pass reviews their model declarations and constraints; model-level examples do not perform instance review.

## Approach

Write the governing Drafts directly, keep the design rationale here, and review the packet before adoption. Preserve Current sources and completed publication history. Resolve exact source-to-Node mappings before replacing Definitions; never replace all `/` edges with composition.

## Results

### What changes

- **Carrier placement is explicit.** Use `@Carrier//Markdown file`. Deliver non-Content Objects into frontmatter. Deliver Content descendants into Markdown. Frontmatter is delimited YAML at the beginning of the file. Carrier filename/location are properties; location is repository-relative.
- **Node scope is explicit.** `Node/**, .**` selects narrower entities plus their Properties. Add `Node` when a rule also covers the root.

- **Names and values use separate expressions.** `p{:0..1}: [format]{:1}` separates occurrence from values. `p.*[...]` constrains immediate names. `p.**[...]` constrains names recursively. Expressions use semicolons.
- **Claim is one Property.** Keep `Atom.Content.Claim`. Formal content is an optional CFEL fence inside its Markdown value. No separate Formal Claim Property is retained. RMED Claim is required. Claim Scope, Semantics and Details are optional.
- **Delivery specifies representation.** `>>` delivers Objects to a referenced Carrier or its parts. Object means Node instance. Filename/location formula details remain separate until expressible.

- **Analysis is freeform.** `Atom.Content.**[string]{:0+}: [markdown]{:1}` constrains each dependent Property recursively. Sibling names are unique. `x.y.z` differs from `x.z`. Shared Atom constraints remain inherited.

- **Graph Syntax becomes CFEL — CAPRMEDIO Formal Expression Language.** CFEL covers expression syntax and meaning for Subject addresses and Formal Claims. Graph, CFEL and Carrier remain distinct model components. This names the existing language; it does not add notation.

- **Declaration is a Form of Requirement.** Use `Role: Requirement / Form: Declaration` and the existing R prefix. Within each selected effective MODEL, each declared member selected by `(Node, Node/**, .**)`, including Properties, has one effective Current Declaration with one matching active Subject. Count only those Declarations; other RMED may address the same Node. Use CFEL Formal Claims where possible. Use Claim prose only for constraints CFEL cannot express. Keep brief Semantics for Primary Nodes only. Each Property Declaration specifies two contracts: direct-value format/cardinality; dependent-entity format/cardinality. Unchanged inherited Properties reuse their original Declaration; explicit MODEL overrides select their local replacement. CFEL entities retain a Claim and may have Semantics.
- **Use Role and Form.** Rename Content Role to Role and the Role-specific Type to Form. These names express different purposes. Naming Methods prefer words that convey the actual distinction and reuse canonical expressions consistently; they do not impose a blanket word ban on useful contextual uses of `content`, `entity` or `type`.
- **Use two root kinds.** MODEL and PROJECT STRUCTURE are Primary Node kinds declared in CAPRMEDIO's self-describing MODEL. Their instance roots are `MODEL//CAPRMEDIO`, `PROJECT STRUCTURE//CAPRMEDIO`, and the corresponding consumer Project roots. The consumer MODEL is optional. PROJECT STRUCTURE describes Scope Structure, Aspects and other declared components. Core Meta-Model contains the Atoms defining CAPRMEDIO's MODEL. Extensible axis configuration stays deferred.
- **Declare Scope outside the constrained Unit.** State permitted active/passive Subjects and Relation endpoints/cardinalities. ENGINE's proposed Scope permits allowed instances and implementation RMED; model definitions use their declared model-defining Scope. A local MODEL does not automatically widen ENGINE's Scope. Target Scope never grants wider authority.
- **Keep graph meanings distinct.** `/` narrows Primary Nodes with inheritance, `//` names their instances, `.` addresses Properties, `+>`/`<+` expresses composition, and `>|`/`|<` expresses classification. Composition uses canonical IS_CONTAINED_BY and derived CONTAINS; Container has yes/no value cases. `(Node, Node/**, .**)` includes the root, its recursive narrower branch and their recursive Properties. `@` references an existing target, parentheses group, and `in (...)` states membership. `:` denotes an allowed value, `=` tests, and `==` establishes a required/derived conclusion. In Subjects, `:=` combines allowed value and condition, as in `Atom/(.Role := Method)`. It does not write an instance value or exclude other allowed values from Atom.Role. Formal Claims keep `:` and `=` separate. Full Formal Claims stay out of Subjects; `..` and an invented `::` meaning are excluded.
- **Keep both counts.** Relation cardinality constrains both written directions; reversal swaps the counts. Property syntax uses separate expressions for occurrence, direct values and immediate dependent names: `p{:occurrence count}; p: [value format]{:value count}; p.*[name format]{:child count}`. YAML and Markdown mappings preserve that distinction, including mixed section content and nested headings.
- **Derive Primary Node versus Property.** The Node branch permits zero or one IS_PROPERTY_OF bearer. Zero derives Primary Node and no direct value; one derives Property and forbids narrowing and instantiation. Property-bearing must be acyclic. HAS_VALUE binds a Property on an instance to a literal, such as CA-P-123.version = 1; literals do not become declared graph Nodes.
- **Inheritance supplies effective rules.** Narrower instances receive applicable Relation cardinalities and declared Property constraints. Do not redeclare an inherited Property or create a new Declaration merely for an inherited lookup. Each Node's single effective Declaration in the selected MODEL resolves its Relation whitelist, endpoint constraints and counts. MODEL inheritance may replace any inherited rule through an explicit local override; unchanged Declarations are reused. Inheritance neither copies instance facts nor gives a Property a second bearer.
- **Operations use siblings and explicit composition.** Workflow, Step, Substep and Action narrow Operations. Each Workflow has one or more Steps, each Step one Workflow. A Step exclusively runs one Action or contains one or more Substeps. Each Substep has one Step and runs one Action. Actions may have zero or more callers. RUN bindings do not establish execution evidence.
- **Store authored instance Relations once.** Rename Subject links to active/passive; store modeled authored Node-instance links under `relations`, with typed containment references. Derive HAS_ACTIVE_SUBJECT from the dedicated Subject field and derive inverse views. The exact Assignee/Target reference migration remains open.

Relation Definitions now state allowed Host/Target signatures and reuse `Direct ((HAS_INVERSE)) Derived`. Inverse views have no separate Definition Atom. Repeated migration commentary is removed from the governing Drafts.

### Why these changes

The human rationale is to remove words that add no useful distinction, keep each complete expression precise, and avoid defining inherited material repeatedly. Primary Nodes, Properties, narrowing, composition and classification need different meanings so the graph can express constraints faithfully. A formal Scope outside its Unit makes the Unit's permitted authority explicit. One Declaration gathers a Node's structure and permissions; formal rules support graph reconstruction without turning an address into a second programming language. Syntax explanations remain useful where symbols are not self-explanatory.

### MODEL and PROJECT STRUCTURE — latest architecture

The two kinds are declared in MODEL//CAPRMEDIO itself. The named Subject roots are their instances:

```text
MODEL//CAPRMEDIO
PROJECT STRUCTURE//CAPRMEDIO
    <+ Scope Structure
    <+ Aspects

MODEL//<PROJECT NAME>              (optional)
PROJECT STRUCTURE//<PROJECT NAME>
    <+ Scope Structure
    <+ Aspects
```

The Project name above is a placeholder. A Project uses MODEL//CAPRMEDIO. It may define a local MODEL. A local MODEL inherits MODEL//CAPRMEDIO and may override any inherited rule. No inherited rule requires an overridable marker.

One Current authoritative Declaration per Node means one effective Declaration within the selected MODEL. Unchanged inherited Declarations are reused. A local replacement and its base source can coexist without becoming two effective owners in that MODEL. This selection context is distinct from the Project-wide instance context used by UNIQUE.

Core Meta-Model is a Scope Unit in CAPRMEDIO's Scope Structure. It contains the governing Atoms defining MODEL//CAPRMEDIO, including the two root kinds. This self-description does not identify the MODEL instance with its Scope Unit or PROJECT STRUCTURE instance. Existing ordered Scope Unit proposals remain subject to exact registration and mapping.

Model inheritance connects MODEL instances. It is separate from `/` Node narrowing and `<+` containment. The inheritance Relation name and exact Model-selection/override binding still need specification; this pass adds no invented notation or runtime behavior.

This replaces the earlier owner-wrapper layout and the MODEL-versus-PROJECT root split. The rationale is to distinguish reusable declarations from each Project's actual structure, reuse inherited material, and let each local MODEL control all of its effective rules.
